# tinyconf

> Go config structs filled from a chain of drivers, every package owns its part of the config and gets its changes without restart

tinyconf fills Go config structs from a chain of drivers by struct tags: defaults, YAML, JSON, TOML, INI, properties, environment variables, flags, Consul, Vault and etcd. The next driver overrides the previous one. Packages parse and subscribe to their own parts of the config, reloads create new versions of the config. The module path is github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2.

# Start

# tinyconf

**tinyconf** is a simple and universal library for parsing configs in Go. It fills your config structs with values from *drivers*: default values from struct tags, YAML, JSON, TOML, INI and .properties files, environment variables, command line flags, Consul KV, HashiCorp Vault, etcd. Every driver is a separate small package, and you can add your own.

One-line ideology

*The config is a plain Go struct. Where the values come from is described by struct tags and by the list of drivers, the last driver wins.*

## Install

```bash
go get github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2@latest
```

Minimum Go version is **1.19**.

## Quick start

```go
package main

import (
    "fmt"
    "time"

    "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2"
    "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/drivers/env"
    "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/drivers/tag"
    "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/drivers/yaml"
    "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/logger"
)

type HTTP struct {
    Host    string        `initial:"localhost" yaml:"host" env:"HTTP_HOST" doc:"http host"`
    Port    int           `initial:"8080" yaml:"port" env:"HTTP_PORT" doc:"http port"`
    Timeout time.Duration `initial:"30s" yaml:"timeout" env:"HTTP_TIMEOUT" doc:"http timeout"`
}

type Config struct {
    HTTP     HTTP     `yaml:"http"`
    Hosts    []string `initial:"a,b" yaml:"hosts" env:"HOSTS" doc:"allowed hosts"`
    Password string   `yaml:"password" env:"PASSWORD" hidden:"true"`
}

func main() {
    tagDriver, err := tag.New("initial") // defaults from the `initial` tag
    if err != nil {
        panic(err)
    }
    yamlDriver, err := yaml.New("config.yaml")
    if err != nil {
        panic(err)
    }
    envDriver, err := env.New()
    if err != nil {
        panic(err)
    }

    // the next driver overrides values of the previous one:
    // defaults < config.yaml < environment variables
    config, err := tinyconf.New(
        tinyconf.WithLogger(logger.NewFmtLogger(logger.INFO)),
        tinyconf.WithDriver(tagDriver),
        tinyconf.WithDriver(yamlDriver),
        tinyconf.WithDriver(envDriver),
    )
    if err != nil {
        panic(err)
    }

    c := &Config{}
    if err = config.Register(c); err != nil {
        panic(err)
    }
    if err = config.Parse(context.Background(), c); err != nil {
        panic(err)
    }
    fmt.Printf("%+v\n", *c)
}
```

With this `config.yaml`

```yaml
http:
  port: 9090
password: secret
```

and `HTTP_HOST=example.com` in the environment the program prints

```text
{HTTP:{Host:example.com Port:9090 Timeout:30s} Hosts:[a b] Password:secret}
```

`Host` came from the environment, `Port` and `Password` from the file, `Timeout` and `Hosts` from the defaults.

# Why tinyconf?

**tinyconf is for Go services built from independent packages, whose config comes from several sources and changes without restart.** Every package declares its own config struct, gets its values and its updates, and knows nothing about the config of the whole application. Where a value came from is always known.

## Who it is for

- **Modular services.** An HTTP server, a database client, a queue consumer, a cache — each package has its own config struct and works with it alone. Adding a package does not touch a central config file of the code.
- **Services that change config at runtime.** A ConfigMap in Kubernetes, keys in Consul or etcd, a rotated secret in Vault: the change reaches only the packages whose part has changed, without restart and without locks in the code that reads the config.
- **Services with many sources.** Defaults, a file, the environment, flags and a remote store at the same time, with one explicit priority order — and an answer to "why is this value here?" when something goes wrong in production.
- **Teams that do not want to maintain config templates by hand.** `.env` examples, YAML templates, flags help and the commands for Consul, Vault and etcd are generated from the same structs.

## What you get

### Every package owns its part of the config

The application registers the whole config once. A package parses, reads and subscribes to its own struct type — no string keys, no `Unmarshal` of a subtree, no knowledge of where its part lives in the whole config.

```go
// in the http package
tinyconf.Current[HTTP](config).Port // the current version: an atomic read, no allocations

tinyconf.Subscribe(ctx, config, func(prev, next *HTTP) {
    server.Restart(next) // called only when HTTP has changed
})
```

Other libraries give one callback for any change of the whole config (viper), or a callback per provider (koanf), and leave it to you to find out what has changed and who should know. See [Sub configs](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/structs/#sub-configs) and [Reloading](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/reloading/index.md).

### Reloads that are safe by design

A reload builds a new version of the config from the defaults. The version that your code holds is never modified, so readers need no locks and never see a half-applied config. A broken file or an unavailable store keeps the last good config; subscribers are called only with a config without errors, and only for their changed part. `ReloadStatus()` reports the last error and the drivers that stopped watching, for health checks. Files are watched by the events of the file system, Consul and etcd notify about changes, Vault is polled.

### One struct, one chain of drivers

The config is your struct, every field says where its value lives:

```go
Port int `initial:"8080" yaml:"port" env:"HTTP_PORT" flag:"http-port" required:"true" doc:"port of the server"`
```

Drivers are applied in the order of addition, the next one overrides the previous one field by field. Eleven drivers out of the box — defaults from tags, YAML, JSON, TOML, INI, properties, environment, flags, Consul, Vault, etcd — and [any file format](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/format/index.md) by a decoder. `time.Duration`, `url.URL`, `TextUnmarshaler`, slices, maps, structs in lists and pointers behave the same in every driver: a conformance test checks it.

### You always know where a value came from

`Sources(conf)` returns the driver and the key of the final value of every field. The debug log shows the initial value of every field, every override and every change after reloads. Secrets are masked everywhere: `hidden:"true"` in the logs and templates, the `tinyconf.Secret` type also in `fmt`, JSON and the logs of the application. See [Value sources](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/sources/index.md) and [Logging](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/logging/index.md).

### Templates of the config from the code

`GenDoc` renders the registered configs with the current values and the `doc` descriptions in the format of every driver: a YAML or TOML file, a `.env` file, flags help, `consul kv put`, `vault kv put` and `etcdctl put` commands. See [Documentation generation](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/gendoc/index.md).

### Light, fast and tested

- No SDKs: Consul, Vault and etcd are used through their HTTP APIs, zap is a separate module. The core depends only on the YAML and TOML parsers, fsnotify and two small libraries of the author, fmap and cast.
- `Current` takes tens of nanoseconds without allocations, `Parse` of a typical config takes microseconds, so the config can be read on every request.
- 100% test coverage, race detector, fuzz tests of the parsers, end-to-end tests with real Consul, Vault and etcd, Go 1.19 and the latest Go in CI, a benchmark diff in every pull request.

### Ready for AI agents

The repository has a [skill for agents](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/ai-agents/index.md) whose programs are built in CI, and the documentation is published as `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` for every version, so an agent writes the code for the current API, not for the one it remembers.

## When another library fits better

- You only read environment variables into a struct — [caarlos0/env](https://github.com/caarlos0/env) or [sethvargo/go-envconfig](https://github.com/sethvargo/go-envconfig) have no dependencies at all.
- You work with config as dynamic keys rather than a struct, or need many remote providers (S3, AWS Parameter Store and AppConfig, Azure Key Vault, NATS) out of the box — pick [koanf](https://github.com/knadh/koanf).
- You are deep in the cobra / pflag ecosystem — [viper](https://github.com/spf13/viper) integrates with them directly.
- You need Go older than 1.19.

## Feature matrix

Checked against the current documentation of the libraries on 2026-10-16.

|                                    | tinyconf                                                                                                             | [viper](https://github.com/spf13/viper)             | [koanf](https://github.com/knadh/koanf)              | [cleanenv](https://github.com/ilyakaznacheev/cleanenv) | [aconfig](https://github.com/cristalhq/aconfig) | [confita](https://github.com/heetch/confita) | [caarlos0/env](https://github.com/caarlos0/env) |
| ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |

| **Defaults in tags**               | ✓ (tag driver)                                                                                                       | ✗ (`SetDefault`)                                    | ✗ (provider)                                         | ✓                                                      | ✓                                               | ✗ (pre-filled struct)                        | ✓                                               |
| **File formats**                   | YAML, JSON, TOML, INI, properties + [any by a decoder](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/format/index.md) | JSON, TOML, YAML, INI, envfile, properties + codecs | many, each a module                                  | YAML, JSON, TOML, EDN, .env                            | JSON + modules                                  | JSON, YAML, TOML                             | ✗                                               |
| **Environment / flags**            | ✓ / ✓                                                                                                                | ✓ / pflag                                           | ✓ / modules                                          | ✓ / ✗                                                  | ✓ / ✓                                           | ✓ / ✓                                        | ✓ / ✗                                           |
| **Remote stores**                  | Consul, Vault, etcd                                                                                                  | Consul, etcd, Firestore, NATS (separate module)     | Consul, etcd, Vault, S3, AWS, Azure, NATS… (modules) | ✗                                                      | ✗                                               | Consul, etcd, Vault, SSM (in core)           | ✗                                               |
| **Required fields**                | ✓                                                                                                                    | ✗                                                   | ✗                                                    | ✓                                                      | ✓                                               | ✓                                            | ✓                                               |
| **Reloading**                      | files by events, Consul and etcd by notifications, Vault by polling                                                  | files by events, remote                             | some providers                                       | manual, env only                                       | ✗                                               | ✗                                            | ✗                                               |
| **Change subscriptions per part**  | ✓                                                                                                                    | ✗ (one global callback)                             | ✗ (one callback per provider)                        | ✗                                                      | ✗                                               | ✗                                            | ✗                                               |
| **Old config untouched on reload** | ✓ (new version)                                                                                                      | ✗ (in place)                                        | ✓ (fresh instance by hand)                           | ✗ (in place)                                           | n/a                                             | n/a                                          | n/a                                             |
| **Where the value came from**      | ✓ driver and key                                                                                                     | ✗                                                   | ✗                                                    | ✗                                                      | ✗                                               | ✗                                            | partial (default or not)                        |
| **Masking secrets**                | ✓ logs, docs, `Secret` type                                                                                          | ✗                                                   | ✗                                                    | ✗                                                      | ✗                                               | ✗                                            | ✗                                               |
| **Generated docs**                 | every driver                                                                                                         | write config back                                   | write config back                                    | env usage                                              | flags usage                                     | flags usage                                  | external tool                                   |
| **Sub configs**                    | by type                                                                                                              | by key                                              | by key                                               | by type                                                | by type                                         | by type                                      | by type                                         |
| **Concurrent use**                 | ✓                                                                                                                    | ✗                                                   | ✗ during load                                        | n/a                                                    | n/a                                             | n/a                                          | n/a                                             |

## Known limitations

- **Fewer remote stores than koanf.** Consul, Vault and etcd only; others need a [custom driver](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/custom/index.md).
- **Vault: AppRole, Kubernetes and token authentication.** Cloud IAM, LDAP and JWT login are delegated to Vault Agent; changes are detected by polling, because Vault does not notify.
- **No HCL out of the box.** The [format driver](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/format/index.md) accepts any decoder, but the conversion of HCL to a map is up to you.
- **Own flag parser.** It ignores unknown flags, so it lives next to cobra or any CLI framework, but it is not a pflag integration.
- **Subscriptions are package functions,** `tinyconf.Subscribe(ctx, config, ...)`, to keep Go 1.19 support; methods with type parameters need Go 1.27.
- **A younger and smaller project** than viper and koanf.

## Migrating

From tinyconf v1: see [Upgrading to v2](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/upgrading/index.md).

| From                                     | To tinyconf                                                                                          |
| ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| viper `SetDefault("http.port", 8080)`    | `initial:"8080"` with the [tag driver](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/tag/index.md)    |
| viper `AutomaticEnv()`                   | [`env.WithAutoKeys()`](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/env/#auto-keys)                  |
| viper `WatchConfig()` + `OnConfigChange` | [`tinyconf.Subscribe`](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/reloading/index.md) per package |
| viper `Sub("http")`                      | `config.Parse(context.Background(), &HTTP{})` or `tinyconf.Current[HTTP](config)`                    |
| cleanenv `env-default`, `env-required`   | `initial:"..."` and `required:"true"`                                                                |
| cleanenv `env-description` + `Usage`     | `doc:"..."` + [`GenDoc("env")`](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/gendoc/index.md)       |
| caarlos0/env `envDefault`, `required`    | `initial:"..."` and `required:"true"`                                                                |

# Use cases

Recipes for typical tasks. Every recipe is a small, complete piece: take the one that matches your application and combine it with others.

| I want to…                                        | Recipe                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| keep defaults next to the fields                  | [Defaults in code](#defaults-in-code)                               |
| configure a service only by environment           | [Environment only](#environment-only)                               |
| have a config file and override it by environment | [File with environment overrides](#file-with-environment-overrides) |
| have different files for dev, stage and prod      | [Files per environment](#files-per-environment)                     |
| ship defaults inside the binary                   | [Embedded defaults](#embedded-defaults)                             |
| keep secrets out of the files and logs            | [Secrets](#secrets)                                                 |
| run in Docker or Kubernetes                       | [Containers](#containers)                                           |
| build a command line tool                         | [Command line tools](#command-line-tools)                           |
| set lists and maps from environment               | [Lists and maps in environment](#lists-and-maps-in-environment)     |
| have a section that can be absent                 | [Optional sections](#optional-sections)                             |
| give every package its own config                 | [Config per package](#config-per-package)                           |
| stop at start if something is missing             | [Fail fast](#fail-fast)                                             |
| apply changes without restart                     | [Reload without restart](#reload-without-restart)                   |
| keep the config in Consul                         | [Config in Consul](#config-in-consul)                               |
| generate an example of the config                 | [Config template](#config-template)                                 |
| find out where a value came from                  | [Debugging](#debugging)                                             |
| test the code that uses the config                | [Tests](#tests)                                                     |
| read values from my own storage                   | [Custom source](#custom-source)                                     |

All recipes use this helper to keep the examples short:

```go
func must[T any](value T, err error) T {
    if err != nil {
        panic(err)
    }
    return value
}
```

## Defaults in code

Default values live in the tags, right next to the fields. The [tag driver](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/tag/index.md) goes first, so every other driver can override it.

```go
type Config struct {
    Host    string        `initial:"localhost"`
    Port    int           `initial:"8080"`
    Timeout time.Duration `initial:"30s"`
    Hosts   []string      `initial:"a,b"`
}

config := must(tinyconf.New(
    tinyconf.WithDriver(must(tag.New("initial"))),
))
```

A value that is computed at runtime can be set in the struct before `Parse`: the field keeps it, if no driver has a value.

```go
c := &Config{Host: must(os.Hostname())}
```

## Environment only

A twelve-factor service without config files. With the [auto keys](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/env/#auto-keys) the `env` tags are not needed, with the [prefix](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/env/#prefix) the variables of the service do not clash with others.

```go
type Config struct {
    HTTP struct {
        Host     string `initial:"0.0.0.0"`
        Port     int    `initial:"8080"`
        MaxConns int    `initial:"100"`
    }
    DatabaseURL string `required:"true" hidden:"true"`
}

config := must(tinyconf.New(
    tinyconf.WithDriver(must(tag.New("initial"))),
    tinyconf.WithDriver(must(env.New(env.WithPrefix("APP_"), env.WithAutoKeys()))),
))
```

```bash
APP_HTTP_PORT=9090
APP_HTTP_MAX_CONNS=500
APP_DATABASE_URL=postgres://db/app
```

## File with environment overrides

The most common setup: defaults, then a file, then the environment on top.

```go
type Config struct {
    HTTP struct {
        Host string `initial:"localhost" yaml:"host" env:"HTTP_HOST"`
        Port int    `initial:"8080" yaml:"port" env:"HTTP_PORT"`
    } `yaml:"http"`
    LogLevel string `initial:"info" yaml:"log_level" env:"LOG_LEVEL"`
}

config := must(tinyconf.New(
    tinyconf.WithDriver(must(tag.New("initial"))),
    tinyconf.WithDriver(must(yaml.New("config.yaml", yaml.WithOptional()))),
    tinyconf.WithDriver(must(env.New())),
))
```

`yaml.WithOptional()` lets the application start without the file at all. Prefer JSON or TOML? The [json](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/json/index.md) and [toml](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/toml/index.md) drivers have the same options, only the tag is different.

## Files per environment

One base file and a small file with differences for every environment. Files are [merged](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/yaml/#several-files): the next file overrides only the keys it has.

```go
stage := os.Getenv("APP_ENV") // dev, stage, prod

yamlDriver := must(yaml.New("config.yaml",
    yaml.WithFiles(
        "config."+stage+".yaml",
        "config.local.yaml", // personal overrides, not in the repository
    ),
    yaml.WithOptional(),
))
```

```yaml
http:
  host: 0.0.0.0
  port: 8080
log_level: info
```

```yaml
log_level: warn
```

```yaml
http:
  port: 9090
log_level: debug
```

## Embedded defaults

Defaults as a readable file that is compiled into the binary, with an optional external file on top. The binary works without any files around it.

```go
//go:embed defaults.yaml
var defaults embed.FS

yamlDriver := must(yaml.New("",
    yaml.WithFS(defaults, "defaults.yaml"),
    yaml.WithFiles("/etc/app/config.yaml"),
    yaml.WithOptional(),
))
```

## Secrets

Three things protect a secret: it is not printed, it is not stored in the file, and the application does not start without it.

```go
type Config struct {
    Database struct {
        Host     string `yaml:"host" env:"DB_HOST"`
        Password string `yaml:"password" env:"DB_PASSWORD" hidden:"true" required:"true"`
    } `yaml:"database"`
}
```

- `hidden:"true"` masks the value in [logs](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/logging/index.md) and removes it from [`GenDoc`](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/gendoc/index.md).
- [`tinyconf.Secret`](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/types/#secrets) instead of `string` masks the value when the application prints or logs the config itself: `%+v`, JSON, zap, slog.
- `required:"true"` makes `Parse` [fail](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/required/index.md) without the value.

Where the value comes from:

```bash
DB_PASSWORD=secret
```

```go
env.New(env.WithSecretFiles())
```

```bash
# the value is read from the file
DB_PASSWORD_FILE=/run/secrets/db_password
```

```go
yaml.New("config.yaml", yaml.WithEnvExpansion())
```

```yaml
database:
  host: db.internal
  password: ${DB_PASSWORD}
```

```go
// add after the file driver: the secret overrides the file
vault.New("app/database", vault.WithKubernetes("app", ""))
```

```go
Password string `yaml:"password" vault:"password" hidden:"true" required:"true"`
```

The driver logs in by the service account of the pod, AppRole and the token of Vault Agent are supported too, see [vault](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/vault/#authentication).

## Containers

A typical Kubernetes deployment: the config file is mounted from a ConfigMap, secrets are mounted as files, a few values are overridden by variables of the pod.

```go
config := must(tinyconf.New(
    tinyconf.WithDriver(must(tag.New("initial"))),
    tinyconf.WithDriver(must(yaml.New("/etc/app/config.yaml",
        yaml.WithOptional(),
        yaml.WithWatchInterval(10*time.Second),
    ))),
    tinyconf.WithDriver(must(env.New(
        env.WithPrefix("APP_"),
        env.WithSecretFiles(), // APP_DB_PASSWORD_FILE=/run/secrets/db_password
        env.WithIndexedKeys(), // APP_HOSTS_0, APP_HOSTS_1
        env.WithFiles(),       // no .env files in the container
    ))),
))
```

```yaml
env:
  - name: APP_DB_PASSWORD_FILE
    value: /run/secrets/db_password
  - name: APP_HOSTS_0
    value: a.example.com
  - name: APP_HOSTS_1
    value: b.example.com
```

A ConfigMap volume is updated by Kubernetes without restart of the pod, so the [reloading](#reload-without-restart) picks up the changes of the file.

## Command line tools

Flags have the highest priority, the file and the environment provide the rest.

```go
type Config struct {
    Output  string   `flag:"output" env:"TOOL_OUTPUT" initial:"out" doc:"output directory"`
    Include []string `flag:"include" doc:"patterns of files to include"`
    Verbose bool     `flag:"verbose" doc:"print debug messages"`
    Help    bool     `flag:"help" doc:"show this help"`
}

config := must(tinyconf.New(
    tinyconf.WithDriver(must(tag.New("initial"))),
    tinyconf.WithDriver(must(env.New())),
    tinyconf.WithDriver(must(flag.New())),
))

c := &Config{}
if err := config.Register(c); err != nil {
    panic(err)
}
if err := config.Parse(context.Background(), c); err != nil {
    fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
    os.Exit(2)
}
if c.Help {
    fmt.Print(config.GenDoc("flag"))
    return
}
```

```bash
tool --output=build --include='*.go' --include='*.md' --verbose
```

The driver [ignores unknown flags](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/flag/#unknown-flags), so it works next to any CLI framework that owns the sub commands and positional arguments.

## Lists and maps in environment

Three forms, from the shortest to the most flexible. All of them fill the same fields:

```go
type Server struct {
    Host string `json:"host" env:"HOST"`
    Port int    `json:"port" env:"PORT"`
}

type Config struct {
    Hosts   []string          `env:"HOSTS"`
    Labels  map[string]string `env:"LABELS"`
    Servers []Server          `env:"SERVERS"`
}
```

```bash
HOSTS=a.example.com,b.example.com
LABELS=env:prod,team:core
```

```bash
HOSTS='["a.example.com","b.example.com"]'
LABELS='{"env":"prod","team":"core"}'
SERVERS='[{"host":"a","port":1},{"host":"b","port":2}]'
```

```bash
HOSTS_0=a.example.com
HOSTS_1=b.example.com
LABELS_env=prod
LABELS_team=core
SERVERS_0_HOST=a
SERVERS_0_PORT=1
SERVERS_1_HOST=b
SERVERS_1_PORT=2
```

The indexed form requires [`env.WithIndexedKeys()`](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/env/#indexed-keys). A value with the separator inside can be quoted, `"a,b",c`, or the separator can be changed with the [`separator` tag](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/tags/#common-tags).

## Optional sections

A feature that is turned on by the presence of its settings. The section is a [struct stored by pointer](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/structs/#structs-stored-by-pointer): it stays `nil` until some driver has a value for one of its fields.

```go
type TLS struct {
    Cert string `yaml:"cert" env:"TLS_CERT"`
    Key  string `yaml:"key" env:"TLS_KEY"`
}

type Metrics struct {
    Addr string `yaml:"addr" env:"METRICS_ADDR"`
}

type Config struct {
    TLS     *TLS     `yaml:"tls"`
    Metrics *Metrics `yaml:"metrics"`
}
```

```go
if c.Metrics != nil {
    go serveMetrics(c.Metrics.Addr)
}
if c.TLS != nil {
    // TLS is enabled, but it can be set partially: check the fields
    if c.TLS.Cert == "" || c.TLS.Key == "" {
        return errors.New("both tls.cert and tls.key should be set")
    }
}
```

Do not use `required:"true"` inside an optional section: a required field is checked even when the section is `nil`, so it makes the whole section mandatory.

## Config per package

Every package declares the struct it needs and does not know about the whole config. The application registers the root config once and passes the manager around.

```go
// package storage
type Config struct {
    DSN      string `yaml:"dsn" env:"STORAGE_DSN" required:"true" hidden:"true"`
    PoolSize int    `yaml:"pool_size" env:"STORAGE_POOL_SIZE" initial:"10"`
}

func New(config *tinyconf.Manager) (*Storage, error) {
    c := &Config{}
    if err := config.Parse(context.Background(), c); err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    return connect(c)
}
```

```go
// package main
type Config struct {
    HTTP    server.Config  `yaml:"http"`
    Storage storage.Config `yaml:"storage"`
}

root := &Config{}
if err := config.Register(root); err != nil {
    panic(err)
}
store := must(storage.New(config)) // parses only the storage section
```

The package gets a [sub config](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/structs/#sub-configs): its own fields with the keys of the whole config, `storage.dsn` in the file.

## Fail fast

Check everything at start and report all problems in one message.

```go
if err := config.Parse(context.Background(), c); err != nil {
    if errors.Is(err, tinyconf.ErrRequired) {
        fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "some required settings are not set")
    }
    fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
    os.Exit(1)
}
```

```text
env driver: field HTTP.Port: failed to parse ... "abc": invalid syntax; field Database.Password: required value is not set
```

`Parse` does not stop on the first error: incorrect values of all fields and all missing [required fields](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/required/index.md) are in the same error.

## Reload without restart

Every package subscribes to its own part of the config, the manager calls it only when this part is changed. See [Reloading](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/reloading/index.md).

```go
c := &Config{}
if err := config.Register(c); err != nil {
    panic(err)
}
if err := config.Parse(context.Background(), c); err != nil {
    panic(err)
}

err := tinyconf.Subscribe(ctx, config, func(prev, next *Logging) {
    if prev.Level != next.Level {
        setLogLevel(next.Level)
    }
})
```

Code that only reads the values takes the current version: `tinyconf.Current[HTTP](config).Timeout`. The versions are never modified, so they are read from any goroutine without locks.

## Config in Consul

The defaults are in the file next to the binary, the settings of the environment are in Consul, and the changes in Consul are applied without restart.

```go
type Config struct {
    LogLevel string `yaml:"log_level" consul:"log_level"`
    HTTP     struct {
        Port int `yaml:"port" consul:"port"`
    } `yaml:"http" consul:"http"`
}

config := must(tinyconf.New(
    // the defaults and the shared document of all instances
    tinyconf.WithDriver(must(yaml.New("config.yaml",
        yaml.WithSource(consul.Document("app/config")),
    ))),
    // separate keys for quick changes: consul kv put app/log_level debug
    tinyconf.WithDriver(must(consul.New("app"))),
))
```

The address and the token are taken from `CONSUL_HTTP_ADDR` and `CONSUL_HTTP_TOKEN`, the same variables the Consul CLI uses. [Subscribe](#reload-without-restart) to apply the changes: Consul notifies the driver right after the change. See [consul](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/consul/index.md).

## Config template

A flag that prints the example of the config and exits. The template is always up to date, because it is generated from the same structs.

```go
c := &Config{}
if err := config.Register(c); err != nil {
    panic(err)
}
if len(os.Args) > 1 && os.Args[1] == "-doc" {
    // fills the defaults and the values of this environment,
    // missing required values are not a problem for the template
    _ = config.Parse(context.Background(), c)
    fmt.Println(config.GenDoc("yaml"))
    fmt.Println(config.GenDoc("env"))
    return
}
```

`GenDoc` shows the current values of the registered config, so after `Parse` the template has the defaults and everything that is set in this environment — it is also a "show effective config" command. Without `Parse` the template has empty values. Fields with `hidden:"true"` are never shown. See [Documentation generation](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/gendoc/index.md).

## Debugging

"Why is the port 9090?" Two tools answer it.

[`Sources`](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/sources/index.md) shows the driver that has set the final value:

```go
for _, source := range config.Sources(c) {
    log.Printf("%s is set by %s driver from %s", source.Field, source.Driver, source.Source)
}
```

```text
HTTP.Host is set by env driver from HTTP_HOST
HTTP.Port is set by yaml driver from http.port
```

The [logger](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/logging/index.md) on the debug level shows the [history](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/logging/#history-of-a-field) of every field: the initial value and every driver that has overridden it, then every change after reloads.

```go
tinyconf.WithLogger(logger.NewFmtLogger(logger.DEBUG))
```

## Tests

Tests should not depend on the files and environment of the machine. Every driver can be fed from memory:

```go
func newTestConfig(t *testing.T, yamlDoc string, args ...string) *Config {
    config := must(tinyconf.New(
        tinyconf.WithDriver(must(tag.New("initial"))),
        tinyconf.WithDriver(must(yaml.New("", yaml.WithData("test", []byte(yamlDoc))))),
        tinyconf.WithDriver(must(env.New(env.WithFiles()))), // no .env files
        tinyconf.WithDriver(must(flag.New(flag.WithArgs(args)))),
    ))
    c := &Config{}
    if err := config.Register(c); err != nil {
        t.Fatal(err)
    }
    if err := config.Parse(context.Background(), c); err != nil {
        t.Fatal(err)
    }
    return c
}

func TestPort(t *testing.T) {
    t.Setenv("HTTP_PORT", "7070")
    c := newTestConfig(t, "http:\n  host: test\n")
    // c.HTTP.Host == "test", c.HTTP.Port == 7070
}
```

To test with a `.env` file without changing the environment of the test process, use `env.WithFiles(path)` together with [`env.WithFilesIsolation()`](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/env/#isolation).

## Custom source

Values from Vault, Consul, a database or any other storage: write a [custom driver](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/custom/index.md). `Load` reads the storage once per `Parse`, `GetValue` converts the values with the `convert` package, so the driver supports the same types as the bundled ones.

```go
type kvDriver struct {
    client *kv.Client
    values map[string]string
}

func (d *kvDriver) GetName() string                       { return "kv" }
func (d *kvDriver) GenDoc(...*tinyconf.Registered) string { return "" }

func (d *kvDriver) Load() (err error) {
    d.values, err = d.client.FetchAll()
    return err
}

func (d *kvDriver) GetValue(field fmap.Field) (*tinyconf.Value, error) {
    key, ok := field.GetTag().Lookup("kv")
    if !ok {
        return nil, tinyconf.ErrIncorrectTagSettings
    }
    raw, ok := d.values[key]
    if !ok {
        return nil, tinyconf.ErrValueNotFound
    }
    value, err := convert.StringToField(raw, field)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    return &tinyconf.Value{Source: key, Value: value}, nil
}
```

Add the `Watch` method of the `tinyconf.Watcher` interface, and the driver takes part in [reloading](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/reloading/index.md).

# Upgrading to v2

v2 changes the module path and a few methods. The steps for the code of v1:

1. Change the imports from `github.com/insei/tinyconf/...` to `github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/...`:

   ```sh
   go get github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2@latest
   ```

1. `Parse` takes the context: `Parse(conf)` is `Parse(context.Background(), conf)`. The context stops the requests of the [remote drivers](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/manager/#parse).

1. The zap adapter is the separate module, zap is not a dependency of the core anymore: `logger.NewZapLogger(l)` is `zaplogger.New(l)` from `github.com/insei/tinyconf/logger/zaplogger`, see [Logging](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/logging/index.md).

1. Fields of an [embedded struct](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/structs/#embedded-structs) without the tag are on the level of the embedding struct, like in `encoding/json`. Check the keys of such fields in the files and the environment variables.

1. `Parse` returns the errors: a value that can't be converted to the type of the field, a file that can't be read, a field with `required:"true"` without a value. v1 only logged them and returned `nil`. All fields are parsed anyway, the errors are returned as one error, see [Errors](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/manager/#errors).

# For AI agents

AI agents often write the code that uses a library, and a model trained before tinyconf v2 does not know its API: it writes `Parse(conf)` without the context or imports `github.com/insei/tinyconf` without `/v2`. Give the agent the current documentation.

## The skill

[`skills/tinyconf/SKILL.md`](https://github.com/Insei/tinyconf/blob/main/skills/tinyconf/SKILL.md) is a short guide for agents in the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format: the rules, complete programs, the drivers with their options and the common mistakes. It is versioned with the code, and CI builds its programs against the code of the repository, so it does not describe the API that does not exist.

Claude Code finds the skill in the `.claude/skills` directory of the project or of the user:

```sh
mkdir -p .claude/skills/tinyconf
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Insei/tinyconf/main/skills/tinyconf/SKILL.md \
  -o .claude/skills/tinyconf/SKILL.md
```

Replace `main` with the release tag, `v2.1.0` for example, to get the skill of the version in your `go.mod`. Other agents read it from any path: mention it in `AGENTS.md` or in the instructions of the agent.

The skill describes the library, not your project. Keep the rules of your project — which drivers you use, where the configs live, how they are registered — in your own instructions next to it.

## llms.txt

The documentation is published in the [llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format for every version:

- [`llms.txt`](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/latest/llms.txt) — the index of the pages with descriptions;
- [`llms-full.txt`](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/latest/llms-full.txt) — the whole documentation as one Markdown file, to put into the context of the agent.

Replace `latest` with the version, `2.1` for example, or with `dev` for the documentation of the `main` branch.
# Features

# Features

Reference of tinyconf capabilities grouped by area.

Looking for a recipe?

The [Use cases](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/use-cases/index.md) page shows how the features work together in typical setups: a twelve-factor service, a config file with overrides, a command line tool, a Kubernetes deployment.

## Configuration

| Page                                                                                             | What's inside                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| [Manager](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/manager/index.md)                        | `New`, `WithDriver`, `WithLogger`, `Register`, `Parse`, priority of drivers, errors, concurrency |
| [Struct tags](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/tags/index.md)                       | Tags of drivers and common tags: `doc`, `hidden`, `required`, `separator`, `kvseparator`         |
| [Supported types](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/types/index.md)                  | Scalars, durations, time, slices, arrays, maps, structs, pointers — the same for all drivers     |
| [Nested structs and sub configs](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/structs/index.md) | Grouping fields into structs, optional sections with pointers, parsing a part of the config      |
| [Required fields](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/required/index.md)               | `required:"true"` tag and `ErrRequired`                                                          |

## Operations

| Page                                                                                      | What's inside                                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Documentation generation](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/gendoc/index.md) | `GenDoc`: a config template in the format of the driver                          |
| [Value sources](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/sources/index.md)           | `Sources`: which driver has set the value of every field                         |
| [Reloading](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/reloading/index.md)             | `Subscribe` and `Current`: configs are parsed again after changes of the sources |
| [Logging](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/logging/index.md)                 | What the manager logs, bundled loggers, custom logger                            |

# Documentation generation

`GenDoc(driverName)` generates a template of the config in the format of the driver: all fields of all registered configs with their descriptions and current values.

```go
c := &Config{}
if err := config.Register(c); err != nil {
    panic(err)
}
if err := config.Parse(context.Background(), c); err != nil {
    panic(err)
}
fmt.Println(config.GenDoc("yaml"))
fmt.Println(config.GenDoc("env"))
```

For this config

```go
type HTTP struct {
    Host string `yaml:"host" env:"HTTP_HOST" initial:"localhost" doc:"http host"`
    Port int    `yaml:"port" env:"HTTP_PORT" initial:"8080" doc:"http port"`
}

type Config struct {
    HTTP     HTTP   `yaml:"http"`
    Password string `yaml:"password" env:"PASSWORD" hidden:"true"`
}
```

the output is

```yaml
#
#http: 
    #http host
    #host: localhost
    #http port
    #port: 8080
#
#password:
```

```bash
#http host
#HTTP_HOST=localhost
#http port
#HTTP_PORT=8080

#
#PASSWORD=
```

- The description is taken from the `doc` tag.
- The value is the current value of the field in the registered config, so call `GenDoc` after `Parse` to get the actual values, or before it to get a clean template.
- Values of the fields with `hidden:"true"` are not shown.
- Slices and maps are shown in the format of the driver: `hosts: ["a","b"]` for yaml, `HOSTS=a,b` for env, so the value can be copied from the template as is.
- The name of the driver is the name of its tag: `yaml`, `json`, `toml`, `ini`, `properties`, `env`, `flag`, `consul`, `vault`, `etcd`. The consul, vault and etcd drivers generate the commands of their CLI, see [consul](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/consul/#documentation), [vault](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/vault/#documentation) and [etcd](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/etcd/#documentation).
- The json and toml drivers generate documents without descriptions, see [json](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/json/#documentation) and [toml](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/toml/#documentation).

A common way to use it is a command line flag of the application that prints the template and exits.

# Logging

The manager logs what happens with every field during `Parse`.

| Level   | Message                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Debug` | `initial`: the value of the field before drivers; `override`: the value is overridden by the driver; `skip`: the driver has no value for the field                                            |
| `Warn`  | the field has no tag of the driver; the driver has found the value in an unexpected place                                                                                                     |
| `Error` | `access denied`: the source denies access to the values, `tinyconf.ErrAccessDenied`; `failed`, `failed to load`, `failed to watch`: the driver failed to get, to parse or to watch the values |

Messages have the fields `config`, `driver`, `field`, `key` and `details` or `value`. Values of the fields with `hidden:"true"` are masked.

## History of a field

On the debug level the log has the whole history of every field: grep the log by the name of the field to see where its value came from.

- At the start of every `Parse` every field is logged with its initial value: the value in the struct before drivers, usually zero.
- Every driver that has changed the value of the field is logged with `override`. A driver that has the same value as the field already has is not logged.
- After every [reload](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/reloading/index.md) only the fields with a new value are logged, with the driver that has set it. Unchanged fields are not logged.

```text
[DEBUG] initial: {config: *main.Config} {field: HTTP.Port} {value: 0}
[DEBUG] override: {config: *main.Config} {driver: tag} {field: HTTP.Port} {key: initial} {value: 8080}
[DEBUG] override: {config: *main.Config} {driver: yaml} {field: HTTP.Port} {key: http.port} {value: 9000}
[DEBUG] override: {config: *main.Config} {driver: env} {field: HTTP.Port} {key: HTTP_PORT} {value: 9090}
...
[DEBUG] override: {config: *main.Config} {driver: env} {field: HTTP.Port} {key: HTTP_PORT} {value: 9091}
```

`field` is the struct path of the field in the registered config, `key` is the place of the value in the source of the driver:

| Driver                            | `key`                                                                                                                                              |
| --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| tag                               | name of the tag, `initial`                                                                                                                         |
| yaml, json, toml, ini, properties | path by the tags, `http.port`                                                                                                                      |
| env                               | name of the variable, with the prefix; `HOSTS_*` for the value from [indexed keys](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/env/#indexed-keys) |
| flag                              | name of the flag, `-http-port`                                                                                                                     |
| consul                            | the key, `app/http/port`                                                                                                                           |
| vault                             | path by the tags, `database.password`                                                                                                              |
| etcd                              | the key, `app/http/port`                                                                                                                           |

If a field has lost its value in all drivers after a reload, it gets its initial value, and it is logged without `driver` and `key`.

## Warnings of drivers

A driver can attach a warning to the value. The value is still used, and the warning is logged with the `Warn` level.

The yaml, json, toml, ini, properties, vault and format drivers warn when a parent of the field has no tag of the driver. The path to the value is built from the tags, so without the tag of the parent the value is read from another key:

```go
type Config struct {
    HTTP struct { // no yaml tag
        Host string `yaml:"host"`
    }
}
```

```text
[WARN] warning: {config: *main.Config} {driver: yaml} {field: HTTP.Host} {details: parent fields HTTP have no 'yaml' tag, the value is read from the 'host' key}
```

Add the tag to the parent, `yaml:"http"`, to read the value from `http.host`.

## Logger from the config

The level, the format or the output of the logger are often a part of the config, but the config is parsed by the manager that already needs the logger. `WithDeferredLogger` breaks this cycle: the manager keeps the log records in memory, and `SetLogger` writes them to the logger created from the parsed config.

```go
config, _ := tinyconf.New(
    tinyconf.WithDriver(tagDriver),
    tinyconf.WithDriver(yamlDriver),
    tinyconf.WithDeferredLogger(), // the records are kept until SetLogger
)
conf := &Config{}
_ = config.Register(conf)
err := config.Parse(ctx, conf)

log := newLogger(conf.Logging)                   // the logger of the application from its config
config.SetLogger(logger.NewSlogLogger(log))      // the kept records are written to it
if err != nil {
    log.Error("config is not parsed", "error", err)
    os.Exit(1)
}

// the logger follows the changes of the config without restart
_ = tinyconf.Subscribe(ctx, config, func(_, next *Logging) {
    config.SetLogger(logger.NewSlogLogger(newLogger(*next)))
})
```

- The records of the first `Parse` get to the logger of the application in its format, its level filters them.
- `SetLogger` is safe for concurrent use with `Parse`, reloads and other goroutines. The records written during `SetLogger` wait for the kept ones, so nothing is lost and the order is kept.
- Up to 1000 records are kept, the oldest are dropped, and the logger gets a warning with the count of the dropped records.
- `SetLogger(nil)` disables logging, the kept records are dropped.
- `SetLogger` replaces the logger set by `WithLogger` too, without `WithDeferredLogger` nothing is kept.

## Bundled loggers

```go
import "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/logger"

// prints to stdout, levels: FATAL, ERROR, WARN, INFO, DEBUG, TRACE
tinyconf.WithLogger(logger.NewFmtLogger(logger.INFO))

// wraps *slog.Logger, Go 1.21 or newer
tinyconf.WithLogger(logger.NewSlogLogger(slog.Default()))
```

The adapter of [zap](https://github.com/uber-go/zap) is a separate module, so zap is not a dependency of tinyconf for the applications with other loggers:

```bash
go get github.com/insei/tinyconf/logger/zaplogger
```

```go
import "github.com/insei/tinyconf/logger/zaplogger"

// wraps *zap.Logger
tinyconf.WithLogger(zaplogger.New(zapLogger))
```

Migration

`logger.NewZapLogger(l)` of the previous versions is `zaplogger.New(l)` from the `github.com/insei/tinyconf/logger/zaplogger` module.

## Custom logger

Implement the `tinyconf.Logger` interface:

```go
type Logger interface {
    Debug(msg string, fields ...Field)
    Warn(msg string, fields ...Field)
    Error(msg string, fields ...Field)
    Info(msg string, fields ...Field)
    With(fields ...Field) Logger
}
```

`tinyconf.Field` is a pair of `Key` and `Value`.

# Manager

`tinyconf.Manager` holds the list of drivers and the registered configs. It is created once at the start of the application.

## Setup

```go
config, err := tinyconf.New(
    tinyconf.WithLogger(logger.NewFmtLogger(logger.INFO)),
    tinyconf.WithDriver(tagDriver),
    tinyconf.WithDriver(yamlDriver),
    tinyconf.WithDriver(envDriver),
)
```

| Option                 | Description                                                                                                                                                               |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `WithDriver(driver)`   | adds the driver, can be used many times                                                                                                                                   |
| `WithLogger(logger)`   | sets the logger, see [Logging](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/logging/index.md)                                                                            |
| `WithDeferredLogger()` | keeps the log records until the logger is set by `SetLogger`, see [Logger from the config](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/logging/#logger-from-the-config) |

## Priority of drivers

Drivers are applied in the order of addition. The next driver overrides values of the previous one, so **the last driver has the highest priority**.

A typical order is: defaults from tags, then files, then environment variables.

A driver overrides the value only if it has a value for the field. A field that is absent in the file keeps the value from the previous driver, and a field without values in all drivers keeps the value that was in the struct before `Parse`.

## Register

```go
c := &Config{}
err := config.Register(c)
```

`Register` takes a pointer to struct. The registered config is used by `Parse` and by [`GenDoc`](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/gendoc/index.md).

## Parse

```go
err := config.Parse(context.Background(), c)
```

`Parse` fills the registered config with values from drivers. The config can be a registered one or a field of the registered config with struct type, see [sub configs](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/structs/#sub-configs). `tinyconf.ErrNotRegisteredConfig` is returned for all other configs.

The context is used by the drivers that read their sources by the network — [consul](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/consul/index.md), [vault](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/vault/index.md), [etcd](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/etcd/index.md) and the remote documents: their requests are stopped when the context is done. A start of the application in Kubernetes is a typical case:

```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Second)
defer cancel()
if err := config.Parse(ctx, c); err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err) // errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) if the storage is not available in time
}
```

Migration

`Parse(conf)` of the previous versions is `Parse(context.Background(), conf)`, and `ParseContext(ctx, conf)` is `Parse(ctx, conf)`.

Every request of the drivers is limited to 30 seconds anyway. The reloads use the context of watching, so the requests are stopped when the last subscription is canceled.

## Other methods

| Method                                 | Description                                                                                                                                               |
| -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GenDoc(driverName)`                   | generates a template of all registered configs, see [Documentation generation](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/gendoc/index.md)             |
| `Sources(conf)`                        | returns which driver has set the value of every field, see [Value sources](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/sources/index.md)                |
| `tinyconf.Subscribe(ctx, m, onChange)` | calls `onChange` after the changes of the config or the sub config, see [Reloading](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/reloading/index.md)     |
| `tinyconf.Current[T](m)`               | returns the current version of the config or the sub config, see [Reloading](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/reloading/index.md)            |
| `ReloadStatus()`                       | state of watching and reloading for the health checks, see [Health checks](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/reloading/#health-checks)        |
| `SetLogger(logger)`                    | replaces the logger, safe for concurrent use, see [Logger from the config](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/logging/#logger-from-the-config) |

## Errors

`Parse` does not stop on the first error: all fields are parsed, and all errors are returned as one error. It can be checked with `errors.Is` and `errors.As`.

```go
if err := config.Parse(context.Background(), c); err != nil {
    // env driver: field HTTP.Port: failed to parse env value from key HTTP_PORT ...
    log.Fatal(err)
}
```

Fields that were parsed without errors are filled even if `Parse` returns an error.

Missing [required fields](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/required/index.md) are reported in the same error and can be checked with `errors.Is(err, tinyconf.ErrRequired)`.

Not an error

A field without a value in the driver and a field without the tag of the driver are not errors, the manager just goes to the next driver.

## Concurrency

All methods of the manager are safe for concurrent use: configs can be registered and parsed from several goroutines. The config struct itself is not protected, do not read it while it is being parsed by another goroutine.

Configs are documented by `GenDoc` and checked for [sub configs](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/structs/#sub-configs) in the registration order.

# Reloading

The manager keeps configs up to date: after every change of the config sources it parses the configs again. The application gets the current version with `Current` and subscribes to the changes with `Subscribe`.

```go
c := &Config{}
if err := config.Register(c); err != nil {
    panic(err)
}
if err := config.Parse(context.Background(), c); err != nil {
    panic(err)
}

// a package subscribes to its part of the config
err := tinyconf.Subscribe(ctx, config, func(prev, next *HTTP) {
    if prev.Timeout != next.Timeout {
        server.SetTimeout(next.Timeout)
    }
})

// anywhere in the application
level := tinyconf.Current[Logging](config).Level
```

## Subscribe

```go
func Subscribe[T any](ctx context.Context, m *Manager, onChange func(prev, next *T)) error
```

- `T` is a registered config or a [sub config](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/structs/#sub-configs): the type of a field of the registered config. A package subscribes to its own part and knows nothing about the whole config.
- `Subscribe` does not block, the subscription is active until `ctx` is done.
- `onChange` is called only if some fields of `T` are changed, with the previous and the new versions. A change of another part of the config does not call it.
- The configs with errors are not applied: the errors are [logged](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/logging/index.md), the subscribers are not called and keep the last good version.

## Current

```go
func Current[T any](m *Manager) *T
```

`Current` returns the current version of the config or the sub config: after the last `Parse` of the registered config or the last reload. It is `nil` before the first `Parse`, and for a sub config stored by pointer that is not created.

Do not change the versions

The versions from `Current` and `onChange` are shared by all readers, so they are read without locks. Never change them: copy the value if it should be changed.

## How it works

- Watching starts with the first subscription and stops after the context of the last one is done. One watching serves all subscribers: every driver watches its sources once for the whole application.
- After every change the registered configs with subscribers are parsed again, **from their values before drivers at the first `Parse`**, so the result is the same as `Parse` would give at the start. A value removed from the file gets its default back.
- All drivers are applied, not only the changed one: the usual [priority of drivers](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/manager/#priority-of-drivers) is kept.
- The new version replaces the current one atomically, and the subscribers of the changed parts are called.
- The config passed to `Register` and `Parse` is never changed in the background, the application can read it as before.
- `Parse` called by the application updates the current version too, but does not call the subscribers: the application knows what it does.
- [`GenDoc`](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/gendoc/index.md) shows the values of the current versions.

## What is watched

Changes are reported by drivers. The bundled [yaml](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/yaml/index.md), [json](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/json/index.md), [toml](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/toml/index.md), [ini](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/ini/index.md) and [properties](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/properties/index.md) drivers watch their files from the OS file system: the main file and the files from `WithFiles`. The [env](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/env/index.md) driver watches its `.env` files. The [consul](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/consul/index.md) driver and Consul documents are notified by Consul right after the change. The [vault](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/vault/index.md) driver checks the versions of the secrets. The [etcd](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/etcd/index.md) driver and etcd documents watch the stream of the events of etcd.

| Source                                    | Watched                                    |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| files from `New` and `WithFiles`          | yes, events of the file system and polling |
| `.env` files of the env driver            | yes, events of the file system and polling |
| Consul keys and documents                 | yes, notified by Consul                    |
| Vault secrets                             | yes, polling, every 30 seconds by default  |
| etcd keys and documents                   | yes, notified by etcd                      |
| files from `WithFS`, data from `WithData` | no                                         |
| process environment, flags, tags          | no                                         |

Files are watched by the events of the file system: inotify on Linux, kqueue on macOS and BSD, ReadDirectoryChangesW on Windows. The change is detected right after the file is written: the driver waits 100 milliseconds for the next events, so the several writes of an editor are one change.

The directories of the files are watched, not the files themselves, so everything that replaces the file works: editors, atomic renames, `kubectl` updates of ConfigMap volumes that replace symlinks. A file that appears or disappears is a change too.

The files are also checked by polling, every 5 seconds by default: it detects the changes when the events are not available — the limit of inotify watches is reached, the directory does not exist yet, the file system does not support events (some network file systems). The interval is set with the `WithWatchInterval` option of the driver:

```go
yamlDriver, err := yaml.New("config.yaml", yaml.WithWatchInterval(time.Minute))
```

## Errors

| Case                                                         | Result                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| the config is not registered                                 | `Subscribe` returns `tinyconf.ErrNotRegisteredConfig`, `Current` returns `nil` |
| no driver can watch for changes                              | `Subscribe` returns `tinyconf.ErrNoWatchers`                                   |
| the new config is parsed with errors                         | the error is logged as `failed to reload`, the current version is kept         |
| a driver can not watch anymore, access is denied for example | the error is logged, other drivers continue watching                           |
| the handler panics                                           | the panic is logged as `subscriber panicked`, other subscribers are called     |

## Health checks

The errors of the reloads are logged, the application keeps working with the last good config. `ReloadStatus` shows this state for the health checks:

```go
status := config.ReloadStatus()
```

| Field            | Description                                                                            |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Watching`       | there are subscriptions and the sources are watched                                    |
| `LastReload`     | the time of the last reload                                                            |
| `LastError`      | the error of the last reload, `nil` if the configs are applied                         |
| `LastApplied`    | the time of the last reload without errors                                             |
| `StoppedDrivers` | the drivers that can not watch anymore, with the errors: access is denied, for example |

A readiness check that fails when the config is broken for a long time or a source is not watched:

```go
func configHealthy(config *tinyconf.Manager) error {
    status := config.ReloadStatus()
    if status.LastError != nil && time.Since(status.LastApplied) > 5*time.Minute {
        return fmt.Errorf("config is not reloaded since %s: %w", status.LastApplied, status.LastError)
    }
    for driver, err := range status.StoppedDrivers {
        return fmt.Errorf("%s driver does not watch for changes: %w", driver, err)
    }
    return nil
}
```

## Details

- Handlers are called one by one in the order of subscription, from one goroutine. The next reload starts after all handlers return, so a slow handler delays the next reload.
- Several changes that happen while the configs are being parsed are merged into one reload.
- On the debug level only the fields with a new value are [logged](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/logging/#history-of-a-field) after a reload, with the driver that has set the value.
- What can be applied on the fly is up to the application: a log level can be changed at any time, a listening port requires restart of the server. Compare `prev` and `next` and act on the fields that matter.

# Required fields

A field with the `required:"true"` tag should have a value. Otherwise `Parse` returns `tinyconf.ErrRequired`.

```go
type Config struct {
    DSN      string `env:"DSN" required:"true"`
    Password string `env:"PASSWORD" yaml:"password" hidden:"true" required:"true"`
    Port     int    `env:"PORT" initial:"8080"`
}
```

```go
err := config.Parse(context.Background(), c)
if errors.Is(err, tinyconf.ErrRequired) {
    // field DSN: required value is not set; field Password: required value is not set
    log.Fatal(err)
}
```

## What is a value

The field passes the check if **any** of these is true:

- some driver has set its value, even if the value is zero: `PORT=0` is a value;
- the field has a non-zero value in the config that was passed to `Parse`.

So a required field without sources can still be filled in the code before `Parse`:

```go
c := &Config{DSN: "postgres://localhost/dev"}
err := config.Parse(context.Background(), c) // DSN is not required to be in the environment
```

## All at once

`Parse` checks all required fields and reports all missing ones in one error, together with the [errors of drivers](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/manager/#errors). The application can show the full list of what should be set in one start, not one variable per attempt.

Defaults and required

A field with a default value in the [tag driver](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/tag/index.md) always has a value, so `required` makes sense only for the fields without defaults: secrets, addresses of external services.

## Sub configs

When a [sub config](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/structs/#sub-configs) is parsed, only its own required fields are checked.

# Value sources

With several drivers it is not always obvious where the final value came from. `Sources` returns which driver has set every field in the last `Parse` call.

```go
if err := config.Parse(context.Background(), c); err != nil {
    panic(err)
}
for _, source := range config.Sources(c) {
    fmt.Printf("%s is set by %s driver from %s\n", source.Field, source.Driver, source.Source)
}
```

```text
HTTP.Host is set by env driver from HTTP_HOST
HTTP.Port is set by yaml driver from http.port
Password is set by env driver from PASSWORD
```

## FieldSource

| Field    | Description                                                     |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Field`  | struct path of the field in the config, `HTTP.Port` for example |
| `Driver` | name of the driver that has set the final value                 |
| `Source` | source of the value inside the driver                           |

`Source` depends on the driver:

| Driver                            | Source                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| tag                               | name of the tag, `initial`                                                                                                                         |
| yaml, json, toml, ini, properties | path by the tags, `http.port`                                                                                                                      |
| env                               | name of the variable, with the prefix; `HOSTS_*` for the value from [indexed keys](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/env/#indexed-keys) |
| flag                              | name of the flag, `-http-port`                                                                                                                     |
| consul                            | the key, `app/http/port`                                                                                                                           |
| vault                             | path by the tags, `database.password`                                                                                                              |
| etcd                              | the key, `app/http/port`                                                                                                                           |

## Rules

- Sources are returned in the order of the config fields.
- Only the last driver that has set the value is reported, the overridden ones are not.
- Fields without values from drivers are not included: they have the value that was in the config before `Parse`.
- Sources are stored per config type, pass the same pointer type that was used in `Parse`. For a [sub config](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/structs/#sub-configs) the paths are relative to it.

It is handy to log the sources once at the start of the application: the answer to "why is this value here" is in the logs. Values themselves are not included, so secrets are not leaked.

# Nested structs and sub configs

## Nested structs

Fields can be grouped into structs. A field with struct type is parsed by its fields, every nested field has its own tags:

```go
type HTTP struct {
    Host string `yaml:"host" env:"HTTP_HOST" initial:"localhost"`
    Port int    `yaml:"port" env:"HTTP_PORT" initial:"8080"`
}

type Config struct {
    HTTP HTTP `yaml:"http"`
}
```

```yaml
http:
  host: example.com
  port: 9090
```

For the yaml driver the tag of the struct field is a key of the nested map, so `Host` is read from `http.host`. Names of environment variables are not built from the parent names: `Host` is read from `HTTP_HOST`, as it is written in its tag.

Types that are parsed from a single value — `time.Time`, `url.URL` and types with `UnmarshalText` — are not nested structs, see [Supported types](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/types/index.md).

## Embedded structs

Fields of an embedded struct without the tag are on the level of the embedding struct, like in `encoding/json`:

```go
type Timeouts struct {
    Read  time.Duration `yaml:"read_timeout"`
    Write time.Duration `yaml:"write_timeout"`
}

type Config struct {
    HTTP struct {
        Timeouts
        Port int `yaml:"port"`
    } `yaml:"http"`
}
```

```yaml
http:
  port: 9090
  read_timeout: 5s
  write_timeout: 10s
```

- The yaml, json, toml, ini, properties, consul, vault and etcd drivers read `Read` from `http.read_timeout`, the embedded struct adds no level. `yaml:",inline"` works the same way.
- With the name in the tag, `` Timeouts `yaml:"timeouts"` ``, the embedded struct is a usual nested struct: `http.timeouts.read_timeout`.
- An embedded struct without the tag is expected, the manager does not [warn](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/logging/#warnings-of-drivers) about it.
- [Auto keys](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/env/#auto-keys) and [indexed keys](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/env/#indexed-keys) of the env driver skip the name of the embedded struct too: `HTTP.Timeouts.Read` is `HTTP_READ` with auto keys, and `SERVERS_0_READ` for the struct in the slice.

## Structs stored by pointer

A struct stored by pointer is parsed the same way, by its fields:

```go
type TLS struct {
    Cert string `yaml:"cert" env:"TLS_CERT"`
    Key  string `yaml:"key" env:"TLS_KEY"`
}

type Config struct {
    TLS *TLS `yaml:"tls"`
}
```

The pointer makes the section **optional**:

- the struct is created when the first value for its fields is found in any driver;
- without values the pointer is not changed, so it stays `nil`;
- an existing struct is filled in place, it is not replaced with a new one.

```go
if err := config.Parse(context.Background(), c); err != nil {
    panic(err)
}
if c.TLS != nil {
    // TLS_CERT, TLS_KEY or the tls section of the file is set
}
```

[Required fields](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/required/index.md) inside such struct are checked even if the pointer is `nil`: a required field makes the whole section mandatory.

Parsed as a single value

Pointers to pointers (`**Struct`) and recursive types (`Next *Node` inside `Node`) are not parsed by fields. They are single values: JSON in string values, a nested map in files.

## Sub configs

A part of the registered config can be parsed separately, by the type of the field. It allows a package to get its own config without knowing about the whole one:

```go
c := &Config{}
if err := config.Register(c); err != nil {
    panic(err)
}

// HTTP is a type of the field in the registered Config
http := &HTTP{}
if err := config.Parse(context.Background(), http); err != nil {
    panic(err)
}
```

The type can be a type of the struct stored by value or by pointer. Only the fields of the sub config are parsed, with the same tags and keys as in the whole config: `http.host` in the file, `HTTP_HOST` in the environment.

If several registered configs have a field with this type, the configs are checked in the registration order and the first found field is used.

# Struct tags

Everything about a field is described by its struct tags: where the value comes from, how it is documented and how it is parsed.

```go
type Config struct {
    Token string   `yaml:"token" env:"TOKEN" initial:"dev" doc:"API token" hidden:"true"`
    Hosts []string `yaml:"hosts" env:"HOSTS" separator:";"`
}
```

## Driver tags

Every driver reads its own tag, the value of the tag is the name of the value in the source of the driver.

| Driver                                                             | Tag                   | Value                            |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| [tag](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/tag/index.md)   | any, set in `tag.New` | the default value itself         |
| [yaml](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/yaml/index.md) | `yaml`                | key in the file                  |
| [json](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/json/index.md) | `json`                | key in the file                  |
| [toml](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/toml/index.md) | `toml`                | key in the file                  |
