| [env](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/env/index.md)   | `env`                 | name of the environment variable |
| [flag](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/flag/index.md) | `flag`                | name of the command line flag    |

A field without the tag of the driver is skipped by this driver.

## Common tags

| Tag               | Description                                                                                                                                                              |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `doc:"text"`      | description of the field for [`GenDoc`](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/gendoc/index.md)                                                                   |
| `merge:"true"`    | slices and maps from several drivers are merged instead of replaced, see [Several drivers](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/types/#several-drivers)         |
| `hidden:"true"`   | the value is masked in logs and is not shown in `GenDoc`, use it for secrets; see also the [`Secret`](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/types/#secrets) type |
| `required:"true"` | `Parse` returns an error if the field has no value, see [Required fields](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/required/index.md)                               |
| `separator:";"`   | separator of slice, array and map items in string values, `,` by default                                                                                                 |
| `kvseparator:"="` | separator of map key and value in string values, `:` by default                                                                                                          |

See [Supported types](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/types/index.md) for the syntax of string values.

# Supported types

All drivers support the same set of types. It is checked by the conformance tests in [`drivers/conformance_test.go`](https://github.com/Insei/tinyconf/blob/main/drivers/conformance_test.go): every type is parsed by every driver, and the results should be equal.

Drivers get values in two forms:

- **string values** — environment variables, command line flags and struct tags;
- **native values** — YAML, JSON and TOML, where lists and maps are a part of the format.

| Types                                                                            | String value                                                | Native value               |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- |
| `string`, `bool`, integers, floats and named types based on them                 | `value`                                                     | scalar                     |
| `time.Duration`                                                                  | `1m30s`                                                     | `1m30s`                    |
| `time.Time`                                                                      | `2024-01-02T03:04:05Z`, `2024-01-02 03:04:05`, `2024-01-02` | the same or yaml timestamp |
| `url.URL`, `[]byte`, any `encoding.TextUnmarshaler` (`net.IP`, `uuid.UUID`, ...) | `value`                                                     | scalar                     |
| `[]T`, `[N]T`                                                                    | `a,b,c`                                                     | list or string             |
| `map[K]V`                                                                        | `a:1,b:2`                                                   | map or string              |
| `[]Struct`, `map[K]Struct`, nested slices and maps                               | JSON: `[{"host":"a","port":1}]`                             | native                     |
| pointers to all types above                                                      | the same                                                    | the same                   |
| `Struct`, `*Struct`                                                              | parsed by fields                                            | parsed by fields           |

## Slices and arrays

```go
type Config struct {
    Hosts []string `env:"HOSTS" yaml:"hosts"`
    Ports [2]int   `env:"PORTS" yaml:"ports"`
}
```

```bash
HOSTS=a.example.com,b.example.com
PORTS=80,443
```

```yaml
hosts: [a.example.com, b.example.com]
ports:
  - 80
  - 443
```

Items that contain the separator can be quoted with double or single quotes: `"a,b",c` is two items. The separator can be changed with the [`separator` tag](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/tags/#common-tags). The number of items for an array should be equal to its length.

## Maps

```go
type Config struct {
    Labels map[string]string `env:"LABELS" yaml:"labels"`
    Limits map[string]int    `env:"LIMITS" yaml:"limits" separator:";" kvseparator:"="`
}
```

```bash
LABELS=env:prod,team:core
LIMITS=cpu=2;memory=512
```

```yaml
labels:
  env: prod
  team: core
limits: {cpu: 2, memory: 512}
```

## Structs in slices and maps

Nested values are set as JSON in string values and as is in YAML, JSON and TOML files:

```go
type Server struct {
    Host string `json:"host" yaml:"host"`
    Port int    `json:"port" yaml:"port"`
}

type Config struct {
    Servers []Server `env:"SERVERS" yaml:"servers"`
}
```

```bash
SERVERS='[{"host":"a","port":1},{"host":"b","port":2}]'
```

```yaml
servers:
  - host: a
    port: 1
  - host: b
    port: 2
```

String values of slices, arrays, maps and structs are parsed as JSON if they start with `[` or `{`. Keys of such structs are taken from the `json` tag for string values and JSON files, from the `yaml` tag for YAML files and from the `toml` tag for TOML files, the field name is used if the tag is not set (case-insensitive).

Fields with struct type

A field with struct type, stored by value or by pointer, is not a single value: it is parsed by its fields, and every field has its own tags. See [Nested structs and sub configs](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/structs/index.md).

## Secrets

`tinyconf.Secret` is a string that is not printed. `hidden:"true"` masks the value in the logs of tinyconf, but the application can print or log the whole config itself; the `Secret` type masks the value there too:

```go
type Config struct {
    Database struct {
        User     string          `env:"DB_USER"`
        Password tinyconf.Secret `env:"DB_PASSWORD"`
    }
}

log.Printf("config: %+v", conf)            // {Database:{User:app Password:******}}
db.Connect(conf.Database.User, conf.Database.Password.Value())
```

- `String`, `GoString` and `MarshalText` return `******` for a not empty value, so `fmt`, `encoding/json`, yaml, zap and slog print the mask. The length of the value is not shown; an empty value is shown as empty, so it is visible that the secret is not set.
- The value is parsed like a usual string by all drivers, slices and pointers of secrets work too.
- `Value()` or `string(secret)` returns the value.
- [`GenDoc`](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/gendoc/index.md) shows `******` as the value of the field.

## Several drivers

If the value of a slice or map is provided by several drivers, the last driver replaces the whole value. With the `merge:"true"` tag the values are merged:

```go
type Config struct {
    Hosts  []string          `initial:"default" yaml:"hosts" env:"HOSTS" merge:"true"`
    Labels map[string]string `initial:"team:core" yaml:"labels" env:"LABELS" merge:"true"`
}
```

```bash
# config.yaml: hosts: [from-file], labels: {env: dev}
HOSTS=from-env LABELS=env:prod
# Hosts:  [default from-file from-env]
# Labels: map[env:prod team:core]
```

- Slices are appended in the order of the drivers, pointers to slices too.
- Maps get the keys of the next drivers, the same key is overridden by the next driver.
- The values of the drivers in one `Parse` call are merged: the first driver with the value replaces the value of the struct, so the next `Parse` does not duplicate the items.
- Arrays, `[]byte` and other types are replaced.
- [`Sources`](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/sources/index.md) reports the last driver, the [log](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/logging/index.md) has every step.
# Drivers

# Drivers

A driver is a source of values. Every driver reads its own struct tag and knows how to find the value for the field in its source.

| Driver                                                                         | Package              | Struct tag                 | Source                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------- | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [tag](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/tag/index.md)               | `drivers/tag`        | any, `initial` for example | default values from struct tags                                   |
| [yaml](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/yaml/index.md)             | `drivers/yaml`       | `yaml`                     | YAML files                                                        |
| [json](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/json/index.md)             | `drivers/json`       | `json`                     | JSON files                                                        |
| [toml](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/toml/index.md)             | `drivers/toml`       | `toml`                     | TOML files                                                        |
| [ini](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/ini/index.md)               | `drivers/ini`        | `ini`                      | INI files                                                         |
| [properties](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/properties/index.md) | `drivers/properties` | `properties`               | `.properties` files of Java and Spring                            |
| [env](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/env/index.md)               | `drivers/env`        | `env`                      | environment variables and `.env` files                            |
| [flag](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/flag/index.md)             | `drivers/flag`       | `flag`                     | command line flags                                                |
| [consul](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/consul/index.md)         | `drivers/consul`     | `consul`                   | Consul KV: a key per field, or a document for yaml, json and toml |
| [vault](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/vault/index.md)           | `drivers/vault`      | `vault`                    | secrets from the KV secrets engine of HashiCorp Vault             |
| [etcd](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/etcd/index.md)             | `drivers/etcd`       | `etcd`                     | etcd: a key per field, or a document for yaml, json and toml      |

Drivers are added to the [manager](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/manager/index.md) with `tinyconf.WithDriver`, the next driver overrides values of the previous one. All drivers support the same [set of types](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/types/index.md).

Need another file format? See [Custom formats](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/format/index.md): a decoder function is enough. Another source? See [Custom drivers](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/custom/index.md).

# consul

The consul package reads the config from [Consul KV](https://developer.hashicorp.com/consul/docs/dynamic-app-config/kv) in two ways:

| Way                             | Where the config is                                  | Tags                                  |
| ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| [key per field](#key-per-field) | every value in its own key: `app/http/port`          | `consul`                              |
| [document](#document)           | YAML, JSON or TOML document in one key: `app/config` | of the format: `yaml`, `json`, `toml` |

Both ways report changes for [reloading](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/reloading/index.md) as soon as they happen: the driver uses [blocking queries](https://developer.hashicorp.com/consul/api-docs/features/blocking) of Consul, not polling. The package talks to the HTTP API of Consul directly and adds no dependencies.

## Key per field

```go
import "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/drivers/consul"

consulDriver, err := consul.New("app")
```

The key of the field is the prefix and the path by the `consul` tags, dots are replaced with slashes:

```go
type Config struct {
    HTTP struct {
        Host string `consul:"host"`
        Port int    `consul:"port"`
    } `consul:"http"`
    Hosts []string `consul:"hosts"`
}
```

```bash
consul kv put app/http/host example.com
consul kv put app/http/port 9090
consul kv put app/hosts a.example.com,b.example.com
```

Values are parsed by the rules of [string values](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/types/index.md), like environment variables: slices are comma separated, structs in slices are JSON.

All keys with the prefix are read by one request once per `Parse` call. A key that is absent is not an error, the field keeps its value from the previous driver.

Set the tags of the parents

The key of the nested field is built from the `consul` tags of its parents. If the `HTTP` field has no `consul` tag, the `Host` field is read from `app/host`, not from `app/http/host`. When a value is found this way, the manager [logs a warning](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/logging/index.md). [Embedded structs](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/structs/#embedded-structs) without the tag are the exception, their fields are on the level of the embedding struct.

## Document

`consul.Document` is a source of the config content for the [yaml](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/yaml/index.md), [json](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/json/index.md) and [toml](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/toml/index.md) drivers. The values are read by the tags of the format driver and merged with the files of the driver, as one more file:

```go
yamlDriver, err := yaml.New("config.yaml",
    yaml.WithSource(consul.Document("app/config")),
)
```

```bash
consul kv put app/config @config.yaml
```

Here `config.yaml` has the defaults, and the document from Consul overrides them. An absent key is an error of `Parse`, unless the format driver has `WithOptional()`.

## Connection

```go
consulDriver, err := consul.New("app",
    consul.WithAddress("https://consul.service:8501"),
    consul.WithToken(token),
    consul.WithDatacenter("dc2"),
    consul.WithHTTPClient(&http.Client{Transport: tlsTransport}),
)
document := consul.Document("app/config", consul.WithAddress("consul.service:8500"))
```

| Option                   | Default                                | Description                                                                                      |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `WithAddress(address)`   | `CONSUL_HTTP_ADDR` or `127.0.0.1:8500` | `host:port` or URL with the scheme; without the scheme `https` is used if `CONSUL_HTTP_SSL=true` |
| `WithToken(token)`       | `CONSUL_HTTP_TOKEN`                    | ACL token                                                                                        |
| `WithDatacenter(dc)`     | the datacenter of the agent            | datacenter of the keys                                                                           |
| `WithHTTPClient(client)` | `http.DefaultClient`                   | client with TLS settings, for example; its timeout should be greater than the wait time          |
| `WithWaitTime(duration)` | 5 minutes                              | maximum time of one blocking query, Consul limits it to 10 minutes                               |

The options are the same for `New` and `Document`.

## Permissions

With ACL Consul hides the keys that the token can not read, and answers as if they are absent. The driver does not let it make the config silently incomplete:

| Case                                              | Result                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| the token can not read the prefix                 | error of `Parse`: `403 Forbidden`                                                  |
| the token can read only some keys with the prefix | error of `Parse`: some keys are hidden by ACL                                      |
| the token can not read the key of the document    | error of `Parse`: `403 Forbidden`                                                  |
| access is denied while watching                   | the driver stops watching, the error is logged: retries do not fix the permissions |

All these errors wrap `tinyconf.ErrAccessDenied`: the manager [logs](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/logging/index.md) them as `access denied`, and they can be checked with `errors.Is`. The token needs `read` on the prefix: `key_prefix "app/" { policy = "read" }`.

## Watching

The manager receives the changes of the keys with the prefix, or of the key of the document, right after they are written to Consul. Keys outside of the prefix do not cause reloads.

If Consul is not available, the driver keeps retrying the requests, with the interval that grows from 1 to 30 seconds, so a restart of Consul does not stop watching. After the failure the config is always reloaded: the changes made while Consul was not available are picked up, even if Consul has lost its data and started its indexes from scratch. The same is true for the start of the application: if Consul is not available at the first `Parse`, the values are loaded by the reloading as soon as Consul is available, and the subscribers are called.

## Documentation

`GenDoc("consul")` generates the commands of the Consul CLI that put the current values to Consul KV, values of `hidden:"true"` fields are empty:

```bash
# http host
consul kv put app/http/host example.com
consul kv put app/http/port 9090
consul kv put app/hosts a.example.com,b.example.com
```

After `Parse` these are the values of the current environment: a way to move the config to Consul. For the document use `GenDoc` of the format driver.

# Custom drivers

Reading config files of another format? A decoder function and the [format driver](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/format/index.md) are enough, no custom driver is needed.

A driver is any type that implements the `tinyconf.Driver` interface:

```go
type Driver interface {
    GenDoc(...*Registered) string
    GetName() string
    GetValue(field fmap.Field) (*Value, error)
}
```

| Method     | Description                                                                                                 |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GetName`  | name of the driver, it is used in logs, errors and as an argument of `Manager.GenDoc`                       |
| `GetValue` | returns the value for the field, it is called for every field of the config                                 |
| `GenDoc`   | returns the documentation of the registered configs in the format of the driver, can return an empty string |

## GetValue

The field is described by [`fmap.Field`](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/insei/fmap/v3#Field): `GetTag()` returns its struct tags, `GetStructPath()` — its path in the config, `HTTP.Port` for example.

The returned value should have exactly the type of the field. To support [the same types](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/types/index.md) as the bundled drivers, use the `convert` package:

- `convert.StringToField(s, field)` — for sources with string values;
- `convert.TreeToField(v, field, tag)` — for values decoded from formats like YAML or JSON.

The returned `tinyconf.Value` has three fields:

| Field     | Description                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Value`   | the value with the type of the field                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `Source`  | the key of the value in the source, `HTTP_PORT` or `http.port` for example; it is returned by [`Manager.Sources`](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/sources/index.md) and logged as `key` |
| `Warning` | optional message for the user, the manager logs it with the `Warn` level; use it when the value is found, but probably not where the user expects                                                     |

Two errors have a special meaning, all other errors are returned from `Parse`:

| Error                              | Meaning                                                                         |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `tinyconf.ErrIncorrectTagSettings` | the field has no settings for this driver, it is skipped                        |
| `tinyconf.ErrValueNotFound`        | the source has no value for the field, the value of the previous driver is kept |

Wrap `tinyconf.ErrAccessDenied` into the error if the source denies access: the token has no permission to read the values. It is still an error of `Parse`, but the manager logs it as `access denied`, so the problem with permissions is not lost among network errors, and the application can check it with `errors.Is`. Return it from `Load`, `GetValue` and `Watch`; `Watch` should stop on it, retries do not fix the permissions.

## Loader

`GetValue` is called for every field. If the source should be read once — a file, a response of the remote service — implement the optional `tinyconf.Loader` interface:

```go
type Loader interface {
    Load() error
}
```

`Load` is called once at the start of every `Parse` call, before any `GetValue` call. If it returns an error, the driver is skipped in this `Parse` call and the error is returned from `Parse`.

A driver that reads its source by the network should implement `tinyconf.ContextLoader` instead: `LoadContext` gets the context of [`Parse`](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/manager/#parse), or the context of watching for reloads, and the requests should stop when it is done.

```go
type ContextLoader interface {
    LoadContext(ctx context.Context) error
}
```

```go
func (d *kvDriver) Load() error {
    values, err := d.client.FetchAll()
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    d.values = values
    return nil
}
```

## Watcher

A driver can report changes of its source for [reloading](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/reloading/index.md) by implementing the optional `tinyconf.Watcher` interface:

```go
type Watcher interface {
    Watch(ctx context.Context, onChange func()) error
}
```

`Watch` should block until the context is done and call `onChange` after every change of the source. The manager parses the config again after the call, so `Load` and `GetValue` should return the new values.

```go
func (d *kvDriver) Watch(ctx context.Context, onChange func()) error {
    events := d.client.Subscribe(ctx)
    for {
        select {
        case <-ctx.Done():
            return nil
        case <-events:
            onChange()
        }
    }
}
```

An error returned before the context is done is logged by the manager, and the driver does not take part in reloading anymore; other drivers continue watching.

## Example

A driver that reads values from a map, the name of the value is taken from the `kv` tag:

```go
type kvDriver struct {
    values map[string]string
}

func (d *kvDriver) GetName() string { return "kv" }

func (d *kvDriver) GenDoc(...*tinyconf.Registered) string { return "" }

func (d *kvDriver) GetValue(field fmap.Field) (*tinyconf.Value, error) {
    key, ok := field.GetTag().Lookup("kv")
    if !ok {
        return nil, tinyconf.ErrIncorrectTagSettings
    }
    raw, ok := d.values[key]
    if !ok {
        return nil, tinyconf.ErrValueNotFound
    }
    value, err := convert.StringToField(raw, field)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse %s: %w", key, err)
    }
    return &tinyconf.Value{Source: key, Value: value}, nil
}
```

```go
type Config struct {
    Port  int      `kv:"port"`
    Hosts []string `kv:"hosts"`
}

config, err := tinyconf.New(tinyconf.WithDriver(&kvDriver{values: map[string]string{
    "port":  "8080",
    "hosts": "a,b",
}}))
```

# env

The env driver reads values from environment variables and `.env` files.

```go
import "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/drivers/env"

envDriver, err := env.New()
```

## Names

The `env` tag is the name of the variable. Names are not built from the names of the parent structs, the variable is read exactly as it is written in the tag:

```go
type Config struct {
    HTTP struct {
        Host string `env:"HTTP_HOST"`
        Port int    `env:"HTTP_PORT"`
    }
    Hosts []string `env:"HOSTS"`
}
```

```bash
HTTP_HOST=example.com
HTTP_PORT=9090
HOSTS=a.example.com,b.example.com
```

Values are parsed by the rules of [string values](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/types/index.md).

## Options

```go
envDriver, err := env.New(
    env.WithPrefix("APP_"),
    env.WithAutoKeys(),
    env.WithSecretFiles(),
    env.WithFiles(".env", ".env.local"),
    env.WithFilesIsolation(),
    env.WithIndexedKeys(),
)
```

| Option                        | Description                                                                          |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `WithPrefix(prefix)`          | adds the prefix to the names of all variables                                        |
| `WithAutoKeys()`              | reads the fields without the `env` tag, the name is built from the path of the field |
| `WithSecretFiles()`           | reads the value from the file, if the variable with the `_FILE` suffix is set        |
| `WithFiles(files...)`         | custom `.env` files instead of the default ones                                      |
| `WithFilesIsolation()`        | does not export the values of the `.env` files to the process environment            |
| `WithWatchInterval(interval)` | the interval of polling the `.env` files for changes, 5 seconds by default           |
| `WithIndexedKeys()`           | reads slices, arrays, maps and structs from separate variables                       |

### Prefix

With `env.WithPrefix("APP_")` the field with the `env:"HTTP_PORT"` tag is read from the `APP_HTTP_PORT` variable. It allows several applications to share one environment and keeps the tags short.

### Auto keys

With `env.WithAutoKeys()` the `env` tag is not required. The name of the variable is built from the struct path of the field:

| Field                                        | Variable         |
| -------------------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `Name`                                       | `NAME`           |
| `HTTP.Port`                                  | `HTTP_PORT`      |
| `HTTP.MaxConns`                              | `HTTP_MAX_CONNS` |
| `DBName`                                     | `DB_NAME`        |
| `HTTP.Timeouts.Read`, `Timeouts` is embedded | `HTTP_READ`      |

The `env` tag still has priority, and the field can be excluded with `env:"-"`.

### Secret files

Docker and Kubernetes mount secrets as files. With `env.WithSecretFiles()` the value can be read from such file: if the `HTTP_TOKEN` variable is not set, but `HTTP_TOKEN_FILE` is set, the value is read from the file with the path from `HTTP_TOKEN_FILE`.

```go
type Config struct {
    Token string `env:"HTTP_TOKEN" hidden:"true"`
}
```

```bash
HTTP_TOKEN_FILE=/run/secrets/http_token
```

The trailing line break of the file content is removed. The variable with the value itself has priority over the file.

### Indexed keys

By default, a slice, a map or a list of structs is set by one variable with the whole value: `HOSTS=a,b` or JSON. With `env.WithIndexedKeys()` every item can have its own variable. It is the form that is natural for Kubernetes manifests and Docker Compose files, where a long JSON in one variable is hard to read and to override.

```go
type Server struct {
    Host     string `env:"HOST"`
    MaxConns int
    Tags     []string
}

type Config struct {
    Hosts   []string          `env:"HOSTS"`
    Labels  map[string]string `env:"LABELS"`
    Servers []Server          `env:"SERVERS"`
}
```

| Type                       | Variables                                                                              |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Hosts []string`           | `HOSTS_0=a`, `HOSTS_1=b`                                                               |
| `Labels map[string]string` | `LABELS_env=prod`, `LABELS_team=core`                                                  |
| `Servers []Server`         | `SERVERS_0_HOST=a`, `SERVERS_0_MAX_CONNS=10`, `SERVERS_0_TAGS_0=x`, `SERVERS_1_HOST=b` |

Rules:

- **Slices and arrays** — the index is added to the name of the field. Indexes should be sequential and start from 0, a gap is an error.
- **Maps** — the rest of the name after the prefix is a key, as is, case-sensitive.
- **Structs** inside slices and maps — names of the fields are taken from their `env` tags or built from the field names: `MaxConns` is `MAX_CONNS`. Fields with `env:"-"` are skipped.
- **Nesting** is not limited: `SERVERS_0_TAGS_0` is the first tag of the first server.
- The variable with the **whole value has priority**: if `HOSTS` is set, `HOSTS_0` is ignored.
- The [prefix](#prefix) is added to all names: `APP_HOSTS_0`.

Names of the map fields

For a map with simple values every variable started with the name of the field and `_` becomes an item of the map. With `Labels` read from `LABELS`, the variable `LABELS_FILE` is the `FILE` key. Choose the name of such field so that it is not a prefix of other variables.

## .env files

By default, `env.New` reads the `.env` files from the directory of the executable and from the working directory and exports their values to the process environment. Absent default files are skipped.

```bash
# comment
HTTP_HOST=example.com
TOKEN="quoted value"
```

- Empty lines and lines started with `#` are skipped.
- Matching single or double quotes around the value are removed.
- Variables that are already set in the process environment are not overridden, so the real environment has priority over the files.

### Custom files

```go
env.New(env.WithFiles(".env", ".env.local"))
```

`WithFiles` replaces the default files. All listed files should exist, otherwise `env.New` returns an error. The value from the previous file has priority over the next files, and the process environment has priority over all files.

`env.WithFiles()` without arguments disables reading of the `.env` files at all.

### Isolation

Exported values are visible to the whole process and to its child processes. With `env.WithFilesIsolation()` the values of the files are available only for the driver, `os.Getenv` does not see them. It is also useful in tests, where the changed environment of the process is a side effect.

### Reloading

The `.env` files are read again before every `Parse`, and they are watched for [reloading](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/reloading/index.md): a change of a file reloads the configs with subscribers. The files are watched by the events of the file system and by polling, as the files of the [yaml](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/yaml/index.md) driver; the default files that do not exist yet are watched too.

```go
envDriver, err := env.New(env.WithFiles(".env"), env.WithWatchInterval(time.Minute))
```

The driver changes only the variables that it exported itself: the new value of the file replaces the exported one, the variable removed from the file is removed from the process environment. Variables set by the environment of the process or changed by the application keep their values. The process environment itself is not watched, it is not changed from the outside of the process.

## Documentation

`GenDoc("env")` generates a commented template of the `.env` file, see [Documentation generation](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/gendoc/index.md). Names of the variables are shown with the prefix, fields without the `env` tag are included if the auto keys are enabled.

# etcd

The etcd package reads the config from [etcd](https://etcd.io) version 3 in two ways:

| Way                             | Where the config is                                  | Tags                                  |
| ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| [key per field](#key-per-field) | every value in its own key: `app/http/port`          | `etcd`                                |
| [document](#document)           | YAML, JSON or TOML document in one key: `app/config` | of the format: `yaml`, `json`, `toml` |

Both ways report changes for [reloading](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/reloading/index.md) as soon as they happen: the driver watches the keys by the stream of the events of etcd, not by polling. The package talks to the [gRPC gateway](https://etcd.io/docs/v3.5/dev-guide/api_grpc_gateway/) of etcd — its JSON API — directly and adds no dependencies.

## Key per field

```go
import "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/drivers/etcd"

etcdDriver, err := etcd.New("app")
```

The key of the field is the prefix and the path by the `etcd` tags, dots are replaced with slashes:

```go
type Config struct {
    HTTP struct {
        Host string `etcd:"host"`
        Port int    `etcd:"port"`
    } `etcd:"http"`
    Hosts []string `etcd:"hosts"`
}
```

```bash
etcdctl put app/http/host example.com
etcdctl put app/http/port 9090
etcdctl put app/hosts a.example.com,b.example.com
```

Values are parsed by the rules of [string values](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/types/index.md), like environment variables: slices are comma separated, structs in slices are JSON.

All keys with the prefix are read by one request once per `Parse` call. A key that is absent is not an error, the field keeps its value from the previous driver.

Set the tags of the parents

The key of the nested field is built from the `etcd` tags of its parents. If the `HTTP` field has no `etcd` tag, the `Host` field is read from `app/host`, not from `app/http/host`. When a value is found this way, the manager [logs a warning](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/logging/index.md). [Embedded structs](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/structs/#embedded-structs) without the tag are the exception.

## Document

`etcd.Document` is a source of the config content for the [yaml](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/yaml/index.md), [json](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/json/index.md) and [toml](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/toml/index.md) drivers. The values are read by the tags of the format driver and merged with the files of the driver, as one more file:

```go
yamlDriver, err := yaml.New("config.yaml",
    yaml.WithSource(etcd.Document("app/config")),
)
```

```bash
etcdctl put app/config < config.yaml
```

An absent key is an error of `Parse`, unless the format driver has `WithOptional()`.

## Connection

```go
etcdDriver, err := etcd.New("app",
    etcd.WithEndpoints("https://etcd-1:2379", "https://etcd-2:2379", "https://etcd-3:2379"),
    etcd.WithAuth("app", password),
    etcd.WithHTTPClient(&http.Client{Transport: tlsTransport}),
)
document := etcd.Document("app/config", etcd.WithEndpoints("etcd:2379"))
```

| Option                        | Default                                                           | Description                                                         |
| ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `WithEndpoints(endpoints...)` | `ETCDCTL_ENDPOINTS` or `http://127.0.0.1:2379`                    | `host:port` or URL with the scheme; the variable is comma separated |
| `WithAuth(user, password)`    | `ETCDCTL_USER` (`user` or `user:password`) and `ETCDCTL_PASSWORD` | the user for the clusters with authentication                       |
| `WithHTTPClient(client)`      | `http.DefaultClient`                                              | the client with TLS settings and client certificates, for example   |

The options are the same for `New` and `Document`, and the variables are the same as etcdctl uses.

Requests go to the next endpoint if the current one is not available, and the endpoint that has answered is used first next time. A cluster keeps working for the application while it has the quorum.

With the user the driver gets the token of etcd and gets it again when the token is expired.

## Permissions

| Case                                           | Result                                                                             |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| authentication is enabled, the user is not set | error of `Parse`: `user name is empty`                                             |
| wrong password                                 | error of `Parse`: `authentication failed`                                          |
| the user can not read the prefix or the key    | error of `Parse`: `permission denied`                                              |
| access is denied while watching                | the driver stops watching, the error is logged: retries do not fix the permissions |

All these errors wrap `tinyconf.ErrAccessDenied`: the manager [logs](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/logging/index.md) them as `access denied`, and they can be checked with `errors.Is`. The role of the user needs `read` on the prefix: `etcdctl role grant-permission --prefix=true app read app/`.

## Watching

The manager receives the changes of the keys with the prefix, or of the key of the document, right after they are written to etcd. Keys outside of the prefix do not cause reloads.

If the stream of the events is broken, the driver watches again from the last known revision, with the interval that grows from 1 to 30 seconds, so no changes are missed. If the history of the changes is already [compacted](https://etcd.io/docs/v3.5/op-guide/maintenance/#history-compaction-v3-api-key-value-database), the config is reloaded from the current state. The same is true for the start of the application: if etcd is not available at the first `Parse`, the values are loaded by the reloading as soon as etcd is available, and the subscribers are called.

## Documentation

`GenDoc("etcd")` generates the commands of etcdctl that put the current values to etcd, values of `hidden:"true"` fields are empty:

```bash
# http host
etcdctl put -- app/http/host example.com
etcdctl put -- app/http/port 9090
etcdctl put -- app/hosts a.example.com,b.example.com
```

After `Parse` these are the values of the current environment: a way to move the config to etcd. For the document use `GenDoc` of the format driver.

# flag

The flag driver reads values from command line flags.

```go
import "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/drivers/flag"

flagDriver, err := flag.New()
```

Add it last, so the flags have the highest priority:

```go
config, err := tinyconf.New(
    tinyconf.WithDriver(tagDriver),
    tinyconf.WithDriver(yamlDriver),
    tinyconf.WithDriver(envDriver),
    tinyconf.WithDriver(flagDriver),
)
```

## Names

The `flag` tag is the name of the flag without dashes:

```go
type Config struct {
    HTTP struct {
        Host string `flag:"http-host" doc:"http host"`
        Port int    `flag:"http-port" doc:"http port"`
    }
    Hosts   []string `flag:"host" doc:"allowed hosts"`
    Verbose bool     `flag:"verbose"`
}
```

```bash
app --http-host=example.com --http-port 9090 --host=a --host=b -verbose
```

A field without the `flag` tag is not read from the command line.

## Supported forms

| Form                              | Example            |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------ |
| `-name=value`, `--name=value`     | `--http-port=9090` |
| `-name value`, `--name value`     | `--http-port 9090` |
| `-name`, `--name` for bool fields | `--verbose`        |

- Bool fields do not take the next argument as a value: use `--verbose=false` to set false.
- Slices and arrays can be filled with repeated flags: `--host=a --host=b,c` is `[a b c]`. For all other types the last occurrence of the flag is used.
- All arguments after `--` are ignored.
- Values are parsed by the rules of [string values](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/types/index.md).

## Unknown flags

The driver does not own the command line: it only looks for the flags of the config fields. Unknown flags and positional arguments are ignored, so the driver can be used together with the `flag` package of the standard library or with any CLI framework.

No --help

The driver does not handle `-h` and `--help`. Print [`GenDoc("flag")`](#documentation) from your own handler of the help flag.

## Custom arguments

By default `os.Args[1:]` is used. Custom arguments are set with `WithArgs`, in tests or for sub commands:

```go
flagDriver, err := flag.New(flag.WithArgs(os.Args[2:]))
```

## Documentation

`GenDoc("flag")` generates the usage of all flags with descriptions from the `doc` tags and current values as defaults:

```text
  -http-host
        http host (default example.com)
  -http-port
        http port (default 9090)
  -host
        allowed hosts (default a,b)
  -verbose
         (default false)
```

Values of the fields with `hidden:"true"` are not shown.

# Custom formats

The format driver reads config files of any format with nested objects. The format is set by a function that decodes the content to a map, everything else is the same as in the [yaml](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/yaml/index.md), [json](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/json/index.md) and [toml](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/toml/index.md) drivers: several files, merging, embedded files, [remote documents](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/consul/#document), environment variables in the content, [reloading](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/reloading/index.md), [documentation](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/gendoc/index.md).

```go
import "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/drivers/format"

driver, err := format.New("hujson", decodeHuJSON, "config.hujson")
```

The name of the driver is the name of the struct tag with the keys, and the name for [`GenDoc`](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/gendoc/index.md):

```go
type Config struct {
    HTTP struct {
        Port int `hujson:"port"`
    } `hujson:"http"`
}
```

## Decoder

```go
type Decoder func(data []byte) (map[string]any, error)
```

The decoder returns the content as a map:

- keys of the map are the keys of the config, nested maps with string keys are nested objects;
- slices are lists, other values are scalars: strings, numbers, booleans, `time.Time`;
- empty content can be decoded to a nil map.

Values are converted to the types of the fields by the same rules as the values of yaml and json, see [Supported types](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/types/index.md).

For example, [HuJSON](https://github.com/tailscale/hujson) — JSON with comments and trailing commas:

```go
import "github.com/tailscale/hujson"

func decodeHuJSON(data []byte) (map[string]any, error) {
    data, err := hujson.Standardize(data)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    var doc map[string]any
    return doc, json.Unmarshal(data, &doc)
}
```

Libraries that decode to the structs only, like HCL, need the conversion of their result to the map.

## Options

| Option                        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `WithFiles(files...)`         | additional files from the OS file system                                                                                                                                                          |
| `WithFS(fsys, files...)`      | files from any `fs.FS`, `embed.FS` for example                                                                                                                                                    |
| `WithData(name, data)`        | in-memory content, the name is used in error messages                                                                                                                                             |
| `WithSource(source)`          | content from a remote storage: [`consul.Document`](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/consul/#document), [`etcd.Document`](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/etcd/#document) |
| `WithOptional()`              | files can be absent                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `WithEnvExpansion()`          | replaces `${VAR}` in the content with environment variables                                                                                                                                       |
| `WithWatchInterval(interval)` | interval of polling the files for [reloading](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/reloading/index.md), 5 seconds by default                                                             |
| `WithEncoder(encode)`         | encoder of the documents for `GenDoc`                                                                                                                                                             |

The rules of the files are the same as in the [yaml](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/yaml/#several-files) driver.

## Documentation

`GenDoc` needs the encoder:

```go
type Encoder func(doc map[string]any) ([]byte, error)

driver, err := format.New("hujson", decodeHuJSON, "config.hujson", format.WithEncoder(func(doc map[string]any) ([]byte, error) {
    return json.MarshalIndent(doc, "", "  ")
}))
```

The document has the same structure as the result of the decoder, with the current values of the registered configs; values of `hidden:"true"` fields are empty strings. Without the encoder `GenDoc` returns an empty string.

## Not a file format?

If the values are not stored as documents — a database, an API, a secret manager — write a [custom driver](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/custom/index.md).

# ini

The ini driver reads values from INI files.

```go
import "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/drivers/ini"

iniDriver, err := ini.New("config.ini")
```

The driver has its own parser and adds no dependencies.

## Keys

The `ini` tag is a key in the file. Tags of [nested structs](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/structs/index.md) are sections:

```go
type Config struct {
    Name string `ini:"name"`
    HTTP struct {
        Host string `ini:"host"`
        Port int    `ini:"port"`
        TLS  struct {
            Cert string `ini:"cert"`
        } `ini:"tls"`
    } `ini:"http"`
}
```

```ini
name = app

[http]
host = example.com
port = 9090

[http.tls]
cert = /etc/tls/cert.pem
```

Dots in the names of the sections and in the keys are nested objects: `[http.tls]` is the `tls` object inside `http`, and `http.port = 9090` in the root is the same as `port = 9090` in the `[http]` section.

Set the tags of the parents

The path of the nested field is built from the `ini` tags of its parents. If the `HTTP` field has no `ini` tag, the `Host` field is read from the `host` key in the root of the file, and the manager [logs a warning](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/logging/index.md). [Embedded structs](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/structs/#embedded-structs) without the tag are the exception.

## Syntax

| Element                              | Example                                |
| ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------- |
| key and value                        | `port = 9090`, `port: 9090`            |
| section                              | `[http]`, `[http.tls]`                 |
| comment                              | `; comment`, `# comment`               |
| comment after the value              | `port = 9090 ; comment`, after a space |
| value in double quotes, with escapes | `name = "my \"app\"\n"`                |
| value in single quotes, as is        | `name = 'my app; # not a comment'`     |
| empty value                          | `name =`                               |

Values of INI are strings, they are parsed by the rules of [string values](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/types/index.md) like environment variables: `true`, `9090`, `1m30s`; lists are comma separated `hosts = a,b`, maps are `labels = env:prod,team:core`, structs in lists are JSON with the keys by the `ini` tags: `servers = '[{"host": "a", "port": 1}]'`. A map can be a section too:

```ini
[labels]
env = prod
team = core
```

A key can not be a value and a section at the same time: `http = 1` and `[http]` in one file is an error of `Parse` with the number of the line.

## Options

The options are the same as of the [yaml](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/yaml/#options) driver:

| Option                        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `WithFiles(files...)`         | additional files from the OS file system                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `WithFS(fsys, files...)`      | files from any `fs.FS`, `embed.FS` for example                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `WithData(name, data)`        | in-memory content, the name is used in error messages                                                                                                                                                               |
| `WithSource(source)`          | content from a remote storage: [`consul.Document`](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/consul/#document), [`etcd.Document`](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/etcd/#document)                   |
| `WithOptional()`              | files can be absent                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `WithEnvExpansion()`          | replaces `${VAR}` in the content with environment variables                                                                                                                                                         |
| `WithWatchInterval(interval)` | interval of polling the files for [reloading](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/reloading/index.md), 5 seconds by default; changes are detected by the events of the file system without waiting for it |

Files are [merged](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/yaml/#several-files) in the order of addition, sections are merged by keys.

## Documentation

`GenDoc("ini")` generates the INI file with the current values: the values of the root first, then the sections of the nested structs. Values of `hidden:"true"` fields are empty, the values that need it are quoted, so the file is read back to the same config.

```ini
hosts = a,b
name = 'my app; with comment chars'

[http]
host = example.com
port = 9090
```

# json

The json driver reads values from JSON files.

```go
import "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/drivers/json"

jsonDriver, err := json.New("config.json")
```

## Keys

The `json` tag is a key in the file. Tags of [nested structs](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/structs/index.md) are keys of nested objects:

```go
type Config struct {
    Name string `json:"name"`
    HTTP struct {
        Host string `json:"host"`
        Port int    `json:"port"`
    } `json:"http"`
    Hosts []string `json:"hosts"`
}
```

```json
{
  "name": "app",
  "http": {
    "host": "example.com",
    "port": 9090
  },
  "hosts": ["a", "b"]
}
```

Options after the comma are ignored: `json:"port,omitempty"` is the `port` key. Set the `json` tag on all parents of the field: without the tag of the parent the field is read from the root of the file, and the manager [logs a warning](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/logging/index.md). [Embedded structs](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/structs/#embedded-structs) without the tag are the exception, their fields are on the level of the embedding struct.

## Options

The options are the same as in the [yaml driver](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/yaml/#options):

```go
jsonDriver, err := json.New("config.json",
    json.WithFiles("config.local.json"),
    json.WithOptional(),
    json.WithEnvExpansion(),
)
```

| Option                        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `WithFiles(files...)`         | additional files from the OS file system                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `WithFS(fsys, files...)`      | files from any `fs.FS`, `embed.FS` for example                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `WithData(name, data)`        | in-memory content, the name is used in error messages                                                                                                                                                               |
| `WithSource(source)`          | content from a remote storage: [`consul.Document`](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/consul/#document)                                                                                                   |
| `WithOptional()`              | files can be absent                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `WithEnvExpansion()`          | replaces `${VAR}` and `${VAR:-default}` in the content with environment variables                                                                                                                                   |
| `WithWatchInterval(interval)` | interval of polling the files for [reloading](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/reloading/index.md), 5 seconds by default; changes are detected by the events of the file system without waiting for it |

Several files are [merged](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/yaml/#several-files) in the order of addition, objects are merged by keys. Files are read once per `Parse` call.

## Documentation

`GenDoc("json")` generates a JSON document with all fields and their current values:

```json
{
  "hosts": [
    "a",
    "b"
  ],
  "http": {
    "host": "example.com",
    "port": 9090
  },
  "name": "app"
}
```

JSON has no comments, so the `doc` tags are not used. Values of the fields with `hidden:"true"` are replaced with empty strings.

# properties

The properties driver reads values from `.properties` files — the format of Java and Spring, `application.properties`.

```go
import "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/drivers/properties"

propertiesDriver, err := properties.New("application.properties")
```

The driver has its own parser and adds no dependencies.

## Keys

The `properties` tag is a part of the key. Tags of [nested structs](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/structs/index.md) are the parts before the dots:

```go
type Config struct {
    Name string `properties:"name"`
    HTTP struct {
        Host string `properties:"host"`
        Port int    `properties:"port"`
    } `properties:"http"`
}
```

```properties
name=app
http.host=example.com
http.port=9090
```

Set the tags of the parents

The key of the nested field is built from the `properties` tags of its parents. If the `HTTP` field has no `properties` tag, the `Host` field is read from the `host` key, and the manager [logs a warning](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/logging/index.md). [Embedded structs](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/structs/#embedded-structs) without the tag are the exception.

## Syntax

The syntax of [`java.util.Properties`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Properties.html#load-java.io.Reader-):

| Element                       | Example                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| key and value                 | `port=9090`, `port: 9090`, `port 9090`                                                  |
| comment                       | `# comment`, `! comment`                                                                |
| escapes                       | `\t`, `\n`, `\r`, `\f`, `\\`, `\uXXXX`; `\` before any other character is the character |
| separators and spaces in keys | `key\ with\=separators=value`                                                           |
| long value on several lines   | a backslash at the end of the line, the leading spaces of the next line are skipped     |

The spaces before the value are skipped, the spaces at the end are a part of the value, like in Java.

Values are strings, they are parsed by the rules of [string values](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/types/index.md) like environment variables: `true`, `9090`, `1m30s`; lists are comma separated `hosts=a,b`, maps are `labels=env:prod,team:core` or the keys `labels.env=prod`, structs in lists are JSON with the keys by the `properties` tags: `servers=[{"host": "a", "port": 1}]`.

A key can not be a value and an object at the same time: `http=1` and `http.port=2` in one file is an error of `Parse` with the number of the line.

## Options

The options are the same as of the [yaml](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/yaml/#options) driver:

| Option                        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `WithFiles(files...)`         | additional files from the OS file system: `application-prod.properties`                                                                                                                                             |
| `WithFS(fsys, files...)`      | files from any `fs.FS`, `embed.FS` for example                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `WithData(name, data)`        | in-memory content, the name is used in error messages                                                                                                                                                               |
| `WithSource(source)`          | content from a remote storage: [`consul.Document`](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/consul/#document), [`etcd.Document`](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/etcd/#document)                   |
| `WithOptional()`              | files can be absent                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `WithEnvExpansion()`          | replaces `${VAR}` in the content with environment variables                                                                                                                                                         |
| `WithWatchInterval(interval)` | interval of polling the files for [reloading](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/reloading/index.md), 5 seconds by default; changes are detected by the events of the file system without waiting for it |

Files are [merged](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/yaml/#several-files) in the order of addition, like the profiles of Spring:

```go
propertiesDriver, err := properties.New("application.properties",
    properties.WithFiles("application-"+profile+".properties"),
    properties.WithOptional(),
)
```

## Documentation

`GenDoc("properties")` generates the file with the current values, sorted by the keys. Values of `hidden:"true"` fields are empty, the special characters are escaped, so the file is read back to the same config.

```properties
http.host=example.com
http.port=9090
name=app
```

# tag

The tag driver takes values right from the struct tags. It is used for default values.

```go
import "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/drivers/tag"

tagDriver, err := tag.New("initial")
```

The argument is the name of the tag with values, any name can be used: `initial`, `default`.

```go
type Config struct {
    Host    string        `initial:"localhost"`
    Port    int           `initial:"8080"`
    Timeout time.Duration `initial:"30s"`
    Hosts   []string      `initial:"a,b"`
}
```

Add it first, so all other drivers can override the defaults:

```go
config, err := tinyconf.New(
    tinyconf.WithDriver(tagDriver),
    tinyconf.WithDriver(yamlDriver),
    tinyconf.WithDriver(envDriver),
)
```

Values are parsed by the rules of [string values](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/types/index.md). An incorrect default value is an error of `Parse`, so a typo in the tag is found at the first start.

The driver has no own documentation format, `GenDoc` returns an empty string for it. Default values are visible in the documentation of other drivers as the values of the fields.

# toml

The toml driver reads values from TOML files.

```go
import "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/drivers/toml"

tomlDriver, err := toml.New("config.toml")
```

## Keys

The `toml` tag is a key in the file. Tags of [nested structs](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/structs/index.md) are names of tables:

```go
type Server struct {
    Host string `toml:"host"`
    Port int    `toml:"port"`
}

type Config struct {
    Name string `toml:"name"`
    HTTP struct {
        Host    string        `toml:"host"`
        Timeout time.Duration `toml:"timeout"`
    } `toml:"http"`
    Hosts   []string          `toml:"hosts"`
    Labels  map[string]string `toml:"labels"`
    Servers []Server          `toml:"servers"`
}
```

```toml
name = "app"
hosts = ["a", "b"]

[http]
host = "example.com"
timeout = "30s"

[labels]
env = "prod"

[[servers]]
host = "a"
port = 1

[[servers]]
host = "b"
port = 2
```

Set the `toml` tag on all parents of the field: without the tag of the parent the field is read from the root of the file, and the manager [logs a warning](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/logging/index.md). [Embedded structs](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/structs/#embedded-structs) without the tag are the exception, their fields are on the level of the embedding struct. Native TOML dates are supported for `time.Time` fields.

## Options

The options are the same as in the [yaml driver](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/yaml/#options):

```go
tomlDriver, err := toml.New("config.toml",
    toml.WithFiles("config.local.toml"),
    toml.WithOptional(),
    toml.WithEnvExpansion(),
)
```

| Option                        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `WithFiles(files...)`         | additional files from the OS file system                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `WithFS(fsys, files...)`      | files from any `fs.FS`, `embed.FS` for example                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `WithData(name, data)`        | in-memory content, the name is used in error messages                                                                                                                                                               |
| `WithSource(source)`          | content from a remote storage: [`consul.Document`](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/consul/#document)                                                                                                   |
| `WithOptional()`              | files can be absent                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `WithEnvExpansion()`          | replaces `${VAR}` and `${VAR:-default}` in the content with environment variables                                                                                                                                   |
| `WithWatchInterval(interval)` | interval of polling the files for [reloading](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/reloading/index.md), 5 seconds by default; changes are detected by the events of the file system without waiting for it |

Several files are [merged](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/yaml/#several-files) in the order of addition, tables are merged by keys. Files are read once per `Parse` call.

## Documentation

`GenDoc("toml")` generates a TOML document with all fields and their current values:

```toml
hosts = ["a", "b"]
name = "app"

[http]
  host = "example.com"
  timeout = "30s"

[labels]
  env = "prod"
```

- The `doc` tags are not used.
- Values of the fields with `hidden:"true"` are replaced with empty strings.
- TOML has no null, so nil pointers and other fields without values are skipped.

# vault

The vault driver reads values from the [KV secrets engine](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/secrets/kv) of HashiCorp Vault.

```go
import "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/drivers/vault"

vaultDriver, err := vault.New("app/config")
```

The driver talks to the HTTP API of Vault directly and adds no dependencies.

## Keys

A secret in Vault is a JSON object. The `vault` tag is a key in it, tags of [nested structs](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/structs/index.md) are keys of nested objects:

```go
type Config struct {
    Database struct {
        Host     string `vault:"host"`
        Password string `vault:"password" hidden:"true"`
    } `vault:"database"`
    Hosts []string `vault:"hosts"`
}
```

```bash
vault kv put -mount=secret app/config - <<'EOF'
{"database": {"host": "db.internal", "password": "secret"}, "hosts": ["a", "b"]}
EOF
```

Values of the secret can be JSON values or strings: `"port": 5432` and `"port": "5432"` are the same for an `int` field, `"timeout": "1m30s"` is a `time.Duration`, see [Supported types](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/types/index.md).

Set the tags of the parents

The path of the nested field is built from the `vault` tags of its parents. If the `Database` field has no `vault` tag, the `Password` field is read from the `password` key in the root of the secret, and the manager [logs a warning](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/logging/index.md). [Embedded structs](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/structs/#embedded-structs) without the tag are the exception.

## Several secrets

```go
vaultDriver, err := vault.New("app/config", vault.WithPaths("app/database", "shared/certificates"))
```

Secrets are merged in the order of addition, like [several files](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/yaml/#several-files): values from the next secret override values from the previous one, nested objects are merged by keys. It is a common layout: the settings and the credentials in different secrets with different access policies.

## Options

```go
vaultDriver, err := vault.New("app/config",
    vault.WithAddress("https://vault.internal:8200"),
    vault.WithTokenFile("/vault/secrets/token"),
    vault.WithMount("kv"),
)
```

| Option                            | Default                                  | Description                                                    |
| --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `WithAddress(address)`            | `VAULT_ADDR` or `https://127.0.0.1:8200` | URL of Vault                                                   |
| `WithToken(token)`                | `VAULT_TOKEN`                            | the token                                                      |
| `WithTokenFile(path)`             |                                          | the file with the token, it is read before every request       |
| `WithAppRole(roleID, secretID)`   |                                          | login by AppRole, see [Authentication](#authentication)        |
| `WithKubernetes(role, tokenFile)` |                                          | login by the service account of the pod                        |
| `WithAuthMount(mount)`            | `approle`, `kubernetes`                  | the mount of the auth method                                   |
| `WithNamespace(namespace)`        | `VAULT_NAMESPACE`                        | the namespace of Vault Enterprise                              |
| `WithMount(mount)`                | `secret`                                 | the mount of the KV secrets engine                             |
| `WithKVv1()`                      | KV version 2                             | read from the KV secrets engine version 1                      |
| `WithHTTPClient(client)`          | `http.DefaultClient`                     | the client with TLS settings, for example                      |
| `WithPaths(paths...)`             |                                          | additional secrets                                             |
| `WithOptional()`                  |                                          | secrets can be absent, by default an absent secret is an error |
| `WithWatchInterval(interval)`     | 30 seconds                               | the interval of checking the secrets for changes               |

The first argument of `New` can be an empty string, if the secrets are set by `WithPaths`.

## Authentication

The driver logs in by AppRole or by the service account of a Kubernetes pod, or uses a token.

### AppRole

```go
vaultDriver, err := vault.New("app/config",
    vault.WithAppRole(os.Getenv("VAULT_ROLE_ID"), os.Getenv("VAULT_SECRET_ID")),
)
```

### Kubernetes

```go
// the token of the service account from /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token
vaultDriver, err := vault.New("app/config", vault.WithKubernetes("app", ""))
```

The second argument is the file with the token of the service account, a projected token with the audience of Vault for example. The file is read before every login, so the token rotated by Kubernetes is used.

The auth methods are mounted at `approle` and `kubernetes` by default, another mount is set by `WithAuthMount("k8s-prod")`.

The driver logs in at the first request and keeps the token. The new token is requested after 2/3 of its lease, and when Vault denies the request: the token can be revoked before its lease expires. Wrong credentials are an error of `Parse` that wraps `tinyconf.ErrAccessDenied`. A login method has priority over `WithToken`, `WithTokenFile` and `VAULT_TOKEN`.

### Token

`WithToken` or the `VAULT_TOKEN` variable set the token. Other methods — cloud IAM, LDAP, JWT — are handled by [Vault Agent](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/agent-and-proxy/agent): it logs in, renews the token and writes it to the file. Point the driver to this file:

```go
vaultDriver, err := vault.New("app/config", vault.WithTokenFile("/vault/secrets/token"))
```

The file is read before every request, so the renewed token is used without restart of the application.

## Errors

| Case                                                              | Result                                                                            |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| the secret is absent                                              | error of `Parse`, unless `WithOptional()`                                         |
| the token can not read the secret, wrong credentials of the login | error of `Parse` that wraps `tinyconf.ErrAccessDenied`, logged as `access denied` |
| Vault is not available or sealed                                  | error of `Parse`                                                                  |

The driver is skipped in the `Parse` call with the error, see [Missing files and values](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/yaml/#missing-files-and-values).

## Reloading

Vault does not notify about changes, so the driver checks the versions of the secrets every 30 seconds while there are [subscriptions](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/reloading/index.md). The interval is set with `WithWatchInterval`. A secret that appears, disappears or becomes available again after an error is a change too.

For KV version 2 the version of the secret is checked, for KV version 1 — the hash of its data.

## Documentation

`GenDoc("vault")` generates the command of the Vault CLI that puts the current values to the first secret, values of `hidden:"true"` fields are empty:

```bash
vault kv put -mount=secret app/config - <<'EOF'
{
  "database": {
    "host": "db.internal",
    "password": ""
  },
  "hosts": [
    "a",
    "b"
  ]
}
EOF
```

# yaml

The yaml driver reads values from YAML files.

```go
import "github.com/insei/tinyconf/v2/drivers/yaml"

yamlDriver, err := yaml.New("config.yaml")
```

## Keys

The `yaml` tag is a key in the file. Tags of [nested structs](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/structs/index.md) are keys of nested maps:

```go
type Config struct {
    Name string `yaml:"name"`
    HTTP struct {
        Host string `yaml:"host"`
        Port int    `yaml:"port"`
    } `yaml:"http"`
}
```

```yaml
name: app
http:
  host: example.com
  port: 9090
```

Options after the comma are ignored: `yaml:"port,omitempty"` is the `port` key.

Set the tags of the parents

The path of the nested field is built from the `yaml` tags of its parents. If the `HTTP` field has no `yaml` tag, the `Host` field is read from the `host` key in the root of the file, not from `http.host`.

When a value is found this way, the manager [logs a warning](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/logging/index.md) with the name of the parent without the tag and the key that was used.

[Embedded structs](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/structs/#embedded-structs) are the exception: they do not need the tag, their fields are on the level of the embedding struct.

## Options

```go
yamlDriver, err := yaml.New("config.yaml",
    yaml.WithFiles("config.local.yaml"),
    yaml.WithOptional(),
    yaml.WithEnvExpansion(),
)
```

| Option                        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `WithFiles(files...)`         | additional files from the OS file system                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `WithFS(fsys, files...)`      | files from any `fs.FS`, `embed.FS` for example                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `WithData(name, data)`        | in-memory content, the name is used in error messages                                                                                                                                                               |
| `WithSource(source)`          | content from a remote storage: [`consul.Document`](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/drivers/consul/#document)                                                                                                   |
| `WithOptional()`              | files can be absent                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `WithEnvExpansion()`          | replaces `${VAR}` in the content with environment variables                                                                                                                                                         |
| `WithWatchInterval(interval)` | interval of polling the files for [reloading](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/reloading/index.md), 5 seconds by default; changes are detected by the events of the file system without waiting for it |

The first argument of `New` can be an empty string, if all sources are set by options.

## Several files

Sources are merged in the order of addition: the file from `New` first, then the sources from options in the order of the options. Values from the next source override values from the previous one, nested maps are merged by keys, all other values — lists too — are replaced.

```yaml
http:
  host: example.com
  port: 80
hosts: [a, b]
```

```yaml
http:
  port: 9090
hosts: [c]
```

```yaml
http:
  host: example.com
  port: 9090
hosts: [c]
```

It is a base for the layered configs: defaults embedded into the binary, the main file, the local overrides.

```go
//go:embed defaults.yaml
var defaults embed.FS

yamlDriver, err := yaml.New("",
    yaml.WithFS(defaults, "defaults.yaml"),
    yaml.WithFiles("/etc/app/config.yaml", "config.local.yaml"),
    yaml.WithOptional(),
)
```

## Missing files and values

A key that is absent in the files is not an error, the field keeps its value from the previous driver.

A file that can not be read is an error of `Parse`, and the driver is skipped in this `Parse` call. With `WithOptional()` absent files are skipped silently, all other errors — a directory instead of the file, incorrect YAML — are still returned.

## Environment variables in files

With `WithEnvExpansion()` the content of the files is processed before decoding:

| Syntax            | Result                                                     |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `${VAR}`          | value of the variable, empty string if it is not set       |
| `${VAR:-default}` | value of the variable, `default` if it is not set or empty |
| `$$`              | the `$` sign                                               |

```yaml
database:
  host: ${DB_HOST:-localhost}
  password: ${DB_PASSWORD}
```

## Reading

Files are read once per `Parse` call, not for every field. The next `Parse` call rereads them, so the changed file is picked up without recreation of the driver.

## Documentation

`GenDoc("yaml")` generates a commented template of the file, see [Documentation generation](https://insei.github.io/tinyconf/2.2/features/gendoc/index.md).
